definition_zh: 演绎的；推论的；从一般到个别的
definition_en: relating to reasoning that moves from general premises to a particular conclusion
core_image: 一排多米诺骨牌从宽大底座一路推到最后一张小牌
scene: 这里指「演绎的」。 The detective's method was deductive: he began with a general rule and narrowed it to one suspect.
sceneCN: 这里 deductive 是「演绎的」（第 1 个义项：从一般规则推出个案结论）；句意：这位侦探的方法是演绎式的：他从一条通则出发，逐步缩小到一名嫌疑人。图中可辨识物件：多米诺骨牌、放大镜、嫌疑人照片、推理板、红色连线。

pos.zh: 演绎的；推论的；运用演绎法的

derivatives.zh: 演绎主义（认为演绎是主要知识方法）

senses.title: From general to particular
senses.titleCN: 从一般到个别：由通则落到个案
senses.definition: reasoning that starts from general premises and derives a particular conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 从一般前提出发推出特定结论的推理
senses.example: The detective's method was deductive: he began with a general rule and narrowed it to one suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 这位侦探的方法是演绎式的：他从一条通则出发，逐步缩小到一名嫌疑人。
senses.why: deducere means 'to lead down'. Deductive reasoning leads a conclusion down from a wide premise to a narrow case, like water channelled from a broad basin into one cup.
senses.whyCN: deducere 意为“引下”。演绎推理把结论从宽泛前提引到狭窄个案，如同水从宽盆引入一只杯子。

senses.title: The deductive method
senses.titleCN: 演绎法：作为研究路径的演绎
senses.definition: a research approach that begins with theory and derives testable predictions
senses.definitionCN: 以理论为起点、推出可检验预测的研究路径
senses.example: The study follows a deductive method, testing hypotheses drawn from theory.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究采用演绎法，检验由理论推出的假设。
senses.why: A method is reasoning made repeatable: the researcher fixes the general premises first, then leads each prediction down in a stated order.
senses.whyCN: 方法使推理可重复：研究者先固定一般前提，再按既定顺序把每个预测引下来。

senses.title: A deductive argument
senses.titleCN: 演绎论证：前提为真则结论必真
senses.definition: an argument whose conclusion follows necessarily from its premises
senses.definitionCN: 结论必然由前提推出的论证
senses.example: A deductive argument can be valid even when its premises are false.
senses.exampleCN: 演绎论证即使前提为假，也可以是有效的。
senses.why: The downward chain is tight: if the premises hold, the conclusion cannot escape. Validity concerns that link, not the truth of the starting points.
senses.whyCN: 这条向下的链条很紧：前提若成立，结论就逃不掉。有效性关乎这一联系，而非起点的真假。

senses.title: Hypothetico-deductive science
senses.titleCN: 假说—演绎：先提假设再推可测结果
senses.definition: describing the scientific pattern in which a hypothesis is proposed and consequences are deduced and tested
senses.definitionCN: 指提出假设、推出后果并加以检验的科学模式
senses.example: The hypothetico-deductive model treats prediction as the test of theory.
senses.exampleCN: 假说—演绎模型把预测当作理论的检验。
senses.why: Science borrows the downward chain twice: first from theory to hypothesis, then from hypothesis to an observable prediction that can fail.
senses.whyCN: 科学两次借用这条向下链条：先从理论到假说，再从假说到可失败的可观测预测。

senses.title: Mathematical proof
senses.titleCN: 数学证明：从公理推到定理
senses.definition: in mathematics, proceeding from axioms or definitions by necessary steps to a theorem
senses.definitionCN: 数学中从公理或定义经必然步骤推到定理
senses.example: The theorem is established by a deductive proof from three axioms.
senses.exampleCN: 该定理由三条公理经演绎证明确立。
senses.why: Mathematics is the home of the pure chain: each step is forced by the one above, with no empirical gap, which is why deductive is strongest there.
senses.whyCN: 数学是纯链条的故乡：每一步都被上一步逼出，没有经验缺口，因此 deductive 在此最强。

senses.title: Deductive closure in epistemology
senses.titleCN: 演绎闭合：已知前提必带出结论
senses.definition: in epistemology, the principle that if one knows a proposition and deduces a consequence, one can know that consequence
senses.definitionCN: 认识论原则：若知道某命题并由之演绎出后果，则也可知道该后果
senses.example: Deductive closure explains why knowledge can extend by inference.
senses.exampleCN: 演绎闭合解释了知识为何能通过推理扩展。
senses.why: If the chain is necessary, then whoever holds the top link holds the bottom one too. Epistemology turns that image into a principle about what a knower may claim.
senses.whyCN: 若链条是必然的，那么握住上端的人也就握住下端。认识论把这个意象变成关于认识者可以主张什么的原则。

senses.title: Detective-style inference
senses.titleCN: 侦探式推断：由线索收窄到唯一
senses.definition: in everyday usage, describing the process of narrowing possibilities by eliminating alternatives
senses.definitionCN: 日常用法中指通过排除其他可能来收窄答案的过程
senses.example: His deductive skills eliminated every suspect but one.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演绎能力排除了除一人之外的所有嫌疑人。
senses.why: Popular writing uses deductive for any neat narrowing, even when the reasoning is really probabilistic. The strict sense requires entailment, not just elimination.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作把 deductive 用于任何漂亮的收窄，即使推理其实是概率性的。严格义要求蕴含，而不只是排除。

senses.title: The deductive-nomological model
senses.titleCN: 演绎—律则模型：用定律解释事件
senses.definition: in philosophy of science, describing an explanation in which an event is deduced from general laws and initial conditions
senses.definitionCN: 科学哲学中指从一般定律与初始条件演绎出事件以作解释
senses.example: The deductive-nomological model places the law at the top of the chain.
senses.exampleCN: 演绎—律则模型把定律放在链条顶端。
senses.why: Explanation becomes deduction: the event is the last domino, and the laws plus initial conditions are the earlier ones that make its fall necessary.
senses.whyCN: 解释变成演绎：事件是最后一张骨牌，定律与初始条件是使之必然倒下的前面那些牌。

intro.en: Deductive is deduct + -ive, built on Latin deducere 'to lead away or down'. It names the direction of reasoning rather than the content.
intro.cn: deductive 是 deduct + -ive，建立在拉丁 deducere“引开、引下”上。它命名的是推理的方向，而非内容。

items.en: deducere 'to lead down or away' combines de- 'down, away' with ducere 'to lead'. The physical image is escorting something from a higher or larger place to a lower or narrower one.
items.cn: deducere“引下、引开”由 de-“向下、离开”与 ducere“引导”组成。其物理意象是把某物从较高或较大处引到较低或较窄处。

items.en: Medieval logicians used the Latin stem for drawing a conclusion from premises. English deduction and deductive entered learned prose in the 16th and 17th centuries.
items.cn: 中世纪逻辑学家用这个拉丁词干表示从前提引出结论。英语 deduction 与 deductive 在16、17世纪进入学术文本。

items.en: The suffix -ive, Latin -ivus, marks a tendency or nature: deductive describes reasoning that has the nature of leading a conclusion down.
items.cn: 后缀 -ive（拉丁 -ivus）标记倾向或性质：deductive 描述具有“把结论引下”性质的推理。

items.en: By the 19th century deductive was fixed in the pair deductive / inductive, naming opposite directions of inquiry.
items.cn: 到19世纪，deductive 已固定于 deductive／inductive 这一对术语中，命名相反的探究方向。

items.en: The 20th century added hypothetico-deductive method and the deductive-nomological model, both extending the downward chain into accounts of scientific practice.
items.cn: 20世纪新增 hypothetico-deductive method 与 deductive-nomological model，把向下链条延伸到对科学实践的说明。

items.en: Whether English deductive came directly from Latin deductivus or was newly formed on deduction is uncertain. The deeper origin of ducere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 英语 deductive 是直接来自拉丁 deductivus，还是在 deduction 上重新构造，存疑。ducere 的更深来源属重构。

note.en: The first group contains forms of the same family with different jobs; the second contains reasoning terms that move in a different direction.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中功能不同的形式；第二组是方向不同的推理术语。

entries.definition: The process or result of deductive reasoning, or an amount subtracted; the noun, not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 演绎推理的过程或结果，或扣除额；是名词而非形容词。

entries.definition: Capable of being inferred; it describes a conclusion, not a method.
entries.definitionCN: 可被推断出来的；描述结论，而非方法。

entries.definition: Tending to bring about a result, as in conducive to health. It shares ducere but leads toward an effect, not down from premises.
entries.definitionCN: 有助于产生某结果的，如 conducive to health。它共享 ducere，但方向是引向效果，而非从前提引下。

entries.definition: Relating to inference of any kind; it covers deduction and induction, so it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 与任何推理有关的；覆盖演绎与归纳，因此更宽。

entries.definition: Reasoning from particular observations to a general rule; the mirror image of deductive.
entries.definitionCN: 从个别观察推出一般规则；是 deductive 的镜像方向。

entries.definition: Relating to the syllogism, a specific two-premise deductive form; narrower than deductive.
entries.definitionCN: 与三段论这一特定双前提演绎形式有关；比 deductive 更窄。

entries.definition: Known independently of experience; deductive reasoning is often a priori, but the terms are not equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 不依赖经验而知的；演绎推理常是先验的，但两个术语并不等同。

entries.definition: Serving to prove or show clearly; it stresses the force of proof rather than the direction of reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 用于证明或清楚展示的；强调证明力度，而非推理方向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: genuine morphology, fixed collocations and the ducere word family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、固定搭配与 ducere 词族。

normal.en: de- 'down' + ducere 'lead' + -ive: an adjective for reasoning that leads a conclusion down from a premise.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ ducere“引导”+ -ive：描述把结论从前提引下的推理的形容词。

normal.en: The pair deductive / inductive is a direction pair: down from the general versus up from the particular.
normal.cn: deductive／inductive 是方向对：从一般向下，从个别向上。

normal.en: Learn deductive reasoning, deductive argument and deductive method; these are the standard academic phrases.
normal.cn: 记住 deductive reasoning、deductive argument、deductive method；这些是标准学术短语。

normal.en: deduction, deduce, deduct, deductive and deductively all carry the duc- core.
normal.cn: deduction、deduce、deduct、deductive、deductively 都带有 duc- 核心。

normal.en: Do not confuse deductive with deducible: one is a method, the other says a conclusion can be drawn.
normal.cn: 不要把 deductive 与 deducible 混淆：一个是方法，一个说结论可被推出。

abstract.en: Picture a row of dominoes starting from a broad base block and ending at one small tile.
abstract.cn: 想象一排多米诺骨牌从宽大的底座开始，到一张小牌结束。

abstract.en: Picture a funnel: many general possibilities pour in at the top, one case comes out at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只漏斗：许多一般可能性从上方灌入，底部只流出一个个案。

abstract.en: Picture a locked chain where pulling the top link necessarily moves the last one.
abstract.cn: 想象一条锁紧的链：拉动最上一环，最后一环必然跟着动。

examples.en: Deductive reasoning moves from a general rule to a specific case.
examples.cn: 演绎推理从一般规则推进到具体个案。

examples.en: The proof is deductive: each step follows necessarily from the previous one.
examples.cn: 这个证明是演绎性的：每一步都必然由前一步推出。

examples.en: Her deductive approach began with theory and ended with a testable prediction.
examples.cn: 她的演绎路径从理论出发，最终得出可检验的预测。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（下）+ duct（管道）+ ive”——像管道一样把结论从上往下输送 → deductive 演绎的、推论的

root: 拉丁 deducere“引下、引开”（de-“向下／离开”+ ducere“引导”）；deduct- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one direction: downward from the general. The chain may run from premises to a case, from theory to a prediction, from axioms to a theorem, or from laws to an event.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个方向：从一般向下。链条可以从前提跑到个案、从理论跑到预测、从公理跑到定理，或从定律跑到事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of dominoes falling from a wide base to one small tile.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排骨牌从宽底座倒向一张小牌。

branches.en: CORE LOGIC: leading a conclusion down from a general rule to a single case.
branches.cn: 核心逻辑：把结论从通则引到个案的过程。

branches.en: RESEARCH: the deductive method and the hypothetico-deductive pattern both start with theory and derive something testable.
branches.cn: 研究：演绎法与假说—演绎模式都从理论出发，推出可检验之物。

branches.en: PROOF AND EXPLANATION: a mathematical proof and a deductive-nomological explanation both make the last step unavoidable.
branches.cn: 证明与解释：数学证明与演绎—律则解释，都使最后一步不可避免。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND DETECTION: deductive closure extends what a knower may claim; detective-style inference narrows suspects.
branches.cn: 知识与侦破：演绎闭合扩展认识者可主张的范围；侦探式推断收窄嫌疑人。

branches.en: VALIDITY: the form matters more than the truth of the premises, which is why a valid deduction can start from falsehoods.
branches.cn: 有效性：形式比前提真假更重要，因此有效演绎可以从假前提出发。

intro.en: Deductive is deduct + -ive, on the Latin participle stem. The suffix marks the nature of the reasoning, while the prefix de- and root duc- are no longer separable in English.
intro.cn: deductive 是 deduct + -ive，建立在拉丁分词词干上。后缀标记推理的性质，而前缀 de- 与词根 duc- 在英语中已不可再分。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere 'to lead' gives a family that includes conduct, induce, reduce, produce, introduce, education and deduct. Each prefixed form specifies a direction, which is why the family is easy to map.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere“引导”衍生出 conduct、induce、reduce、produce、introduce、education、deduct 等词族。每个带前缀形式都指定方向，因此这个词族容易画成地图。

items.meaningCN: 从一般到个别的演绎推理（-ive 表性质）
items.example: The course teaches deductive and inductive logic.
items.exampleCN: 这门课教授演绎逻辑与归纳逻辑。

items.meaning: the act or result of deducing; a subtraction
items.meaningCN: 演绎；推论；扣除（-ion 表行为或结果）
items.example: The deduction is valid but unsound.
items.exampleCN: 这个演绎有效但不可靠（前提不真）。

items.meaningCN: 推断；演绎（de-“向下”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: From the map we deduced the old boundary.
items.exampleCN: 我们从地图推断出旧边界。

items.example: Tax is deducted before the salary is paid.
items.exampleCN: 税款在发薪前扣除。

items.meaningCN: 以演绎方式（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The conclusion was reached deductively.
items.exampleCN: 该结论是以演绎方式得出的。

items.meaning: the view that deduction is the main route to knowledge
items.meaningCN: 演绎主义：认为演绎是主要知识路径（-ism 表主义）
items.example: Deductivism overstates the role of axioms.
items.exampleCN: 演绎主义夸大了公理的作用。

items.meaning: to lead into; to infer a general rule
items.meaningCN: 诱导；归纳（in-“进入”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: They induced a rule from repeated observations.
items.exampleCN: 他们从反复观察中归纳出一条规则。

items.example: The model reduces the problem to two variables.
items.exampleCN: 该模型把问题化简为两个变量。

items.meaning: to lead, guide, or carry out
items.meaningCN: 引导；进行（con-“一起”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The team conducted the trial in three hospitals.
items.exampleCN: 团队在三家医院开展了试验。

latinEntries.meaning: serving to lead out or infer (Medieval Latin)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用于引出或推断的（中世纪拉丁）

latinEntries.meaning: a leading away; a drawing out

definition_zh: 例行地；按常规地；通常
definition_en: in the usual fixed way, as a regular part of what is done
core_image: 值班表上同一格被反复勾上，勾的人连笔都没有停，心里已经想到了下一件事
scene: 清晨的实验室里，同一批样本被依次编号、离心、记录，操作者没有翻看手册，也没有停顿。 The samples were routinely checked for contamination before storage.
sceneCN: 这里本词作副词，表示动作按既定流程反复进行（第 1 个义项：按常规例行地）；句意为样本入库前都会照例做污染检查。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀后得到基础词，语义为「惯例、固定流程」
由基础词加表「使…化」的动词后缀构成，语义偏移为「使成为固定流程」
由上一动词再加表过程的名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「流程化」
由基础词加表「人」的后缀构成，语义偏移为「只按旧例办事的人」

senses.title: As a matter of fixed practice
senses.definition: in the fixed order established for a task, without variation
senses.definitionCN: 按某项工作已经定下的固定次序、不作变动地
senses.example: Visitors are routinely asked to sign in at the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 来访者照例会被告知在前台登记。
senses.why: The adverb adds the manner suffix to the noun of habit, so it describes doing something in that habitual way.
senses.whyCN: 副词在表习惯的名词后加了表方式的后缀，因此描述以那种惯常方式做事。

senses.title: Usually, in most cases
senses.definition: in most cases, as the ordinary state of affairs
senses.definitionCN: 在多数情况下，作为寻常状况
senses.example: Such delays are routinely reported in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这类延误在冬季通常都会被报道。
senses.why: What happens by habit happens most of the time, so the adverb slid from manner into frequency.
senses.whyCN: 按习惯发生的事多半时候都会发生，副词于是从方式义滑向频率义。

senses.title: Mechanically, without reflection
senses.definition: by force of habit, with no fresh attention to what is being done
senses.definitionCN: 凭习惯去做，对正在做的事不再重新留意
senses.example: He routinely signed papers he had not read.
senses.exampleCN: 他机械地签下自己没读过的文件。
senses.why: A path walked without looking turns the act into a reflex, and the adverb carries that blankness.
senses.whyCN: 不看路地走会把动作变成反射，副词也带上了这种空白感。

senses.title: Every day, as a daily matter
senses.definition: on each day, as part of the daily order
senses.definitionCN: 每一天都如此，作为每日安排的一部分
senses.example: The tide gauge is routinely read at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 潮位计每天清晨照例被读取。
senses.why: The daily round is the oldest sense of the noun, and the adverb keeps its calendar.
senses.whyCN: 每日循环是名词最古老的义项，副词也保留着这层日历意味。

senses.title: Systematically, as a set procedure
senses.definition: as part of an organised procedure applied to every case
senses.definitionCN: 作为一套有组织的程序，对每一个对象都照此执行
senses.example: Every batch is routinely screened for the same three metals.
senses.exampleCN: 每一批都按程序筛查同样的三种金属。
senses.why: A procedure that covers all cases makes the act systematic, and the adverb marks that coverage.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖所有对象的程序使行为变得系统，副词标记的正是这种覆盖。

senses.title: At regular intervals
senses.definition: at fixed intervals of time rather than once
senses.definitionCN: 按固定的时间间隔进行，而非只做一次
senses.example: The filters are routinely replaced every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 滤芯每季度定期更换。
senses.why: A repeated path has a rhythm, and the adverb can name that rhythm rather than the habit itself.
senses.whyCN: 重复的路径带有节拍，副词可以指这种节拍而不只是习惯本身。

senses.title: Commonly, as a general rule
senses.definition: as the general rule that most people or cases follow
senses.definitionCN: 作为多数人或多数情况都遵循的一般规则
senses.example: Economists routinely expect such shocks to fade.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家普遍预期这类冲击会消退。
senses.why: When nearly everyone follows a path, the adverb describes the general rule rather than one person's habit.
senses.whyCN: 当几乎人人都走这条路，副词描述的是通则，而非某人的习惯。

senses.title: By institutional custom
senses.definition: according to the unwritten custom of an organisation rather than a written rule
senses.definitionCN: 依照某个组织不成文的惯例，而非依成文规定
senses.example: The committee routinely meets behind closed doors.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会按惯例闭门开会。
senses.why: Institutions run on paths no one wrote down, and the adverb names that quiet custom.
senses.whyCN: 机构靠没人写下来的路径运转，副词指的就是这种无声惯例。

intro.en: Routinely is the noun routine with the English adverb suffix, and routine itself came from French, which drew it from a Latin phrase for an opened way.
intro.cn: 本词是表「惯例」的名词加英语副词后缀构成；而那个名词来自法语，法语又取自拉丁语中表「被开出的路」的词组。

items.en: The Latin phrase meant a way broken open or cleared through, the image behind the French word for a road.
items.cn: 这一拉丁词组意为「被开出、被清理出来的路」，是法语表「道路」一词背后的意象。

items.en: French kept the road sense and later built a noun for the habit of taking the same way.
items.cn: 法语保留了「道路」义，后来又造出表「惯走同一条路」的名词。

items.en: The French noun named a settled habit of acting, a way of doing things that repeats.
items.cn: 这个法语名词指固定的行事习惯，即反复使用的一种做事方式。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the eighteenth century for an established order of actions.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入该名词，指已确立的行事次序。

items.en: English added its native manner suffix to the borrowed noun and produced an adverb that soon also meant usually.
items.cn: 英语在借入的名词后加上本族表方式的后缀，造出副词，很快又带上「通常」的意思。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the Latin phrase is usually reconstructed from a verb meaning to break, and the first English adverb citation is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一拉丁词组的更深来源通常由表「破开」的动词重构，该副词最早的书证年代亦无确说。

note.en: Group one collects the noun and its near forms that share letters with the adverb; group two collects adverbs of regularity and frequency.
note.cn: 第一组是与副词共享字母的名词及其近形词；第二组是表示规律与频率的副词。

entries.definition: The base noun and adjective names the fixed order itself, while the adverb names the manner of doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 作为基础的名词与形容词指固定次序本身，副词则指做事的方式。

entries.tag: verb to fix into a procedure
entries.definition: A verb built on the same noun: it means turning an activity into a set procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一名词构成的动词，意为把某项活动变成固定程序。

entries.definition: A noun for someone who follows routine mechanically, with a person suffix rather than an adverb suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 指机械照旧例办事的人，用的是表「人」的后缀而非副词后缀。

entries.definition: A relative from the same Latin phrase, but it is the path, not the way of walking it.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个拉丁词组的同源词，但它指路径，不指走它的方式。

entries.definition: At set times or intervals; the emphasis is on the timetable rather than on the absence of thought.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定时间或间隔进行，强调时间表而非不加思索。

entries.definition: Out of a settled personal habit, often with a hint of blame that routine does not always carry.
entries.definitionCN: 出于固定的个人习惯，常带一点责备意味，而本词未必带。

entries.definition: As the usual state of things among many people or cases, with no suggestion of a fixed procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指许多人或许多情况中的寻常状态，并不暗示固定程序。

entries.definition: By an organised method that covers every case, stressing design rather than mere repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 按覆盖每一例的有组织方法，强调设计而非单纯重复。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base noun means a habitual path; the adverb suffix turns that into the manner of walking it.
normal.cn: 基础名词指惯常的路径，副词后缀把它转成走这条路的方式。

normal.en: The family runs routine, routinely, routinize, routinization, routineer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括惯例、按常规地、使流程化、流程化与墨守成规者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: routinely checked, routinely collected, routinely ignored, routinely tested.
normal.cn: 固定说法：例行检查、例行采集、通常被忽略、定期检测。

normal.en: The adverb can describe a timetable, a frequency or a blank habit, depending on the sentence.
normal.cn: 这个副词可以指时间表、频率或不带思考的习惯，视句子而定。

normal.en: Compare it with the adjective and the noun: the same root, three different jobs.
normal.cn: 把它与形容词、名词对照：同一个词根，三种不同的功用。

abstract.en: Picture a clipboard where the same line is ticked before the reader reaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写字板，读的人还没读到那一行，勾已经先打上了。

abstract.en: Picture a conveyor belt that never pauses for anyone to think.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从不为任何人思考而停下的传送带。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands move while nobody in the room looks up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟的指针在走，屋里没人抬头看。

examples.en: Nurses routinely weigh every patient on admission.
examples.cn: 护士照例给每位入院病人称体重。

examples.en: Critics are routinely dismissed as complainers.
examples.cn: 批评者通常被当作抱怨者打发掉。

examples.en: The server is routinely backed up at midnight.
examples.cn: 服务器每天午夜按惯例备份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「惯例」与表方式的后缀合起来看：以惯常的方式去做，就是照例、照常。

root: 由表「惯例」的名词加英语副词后缀构成；那个名词来自法语，更早出自拉丁语「被开出的路」的词组，引申为反复走成的固定做法；更深来源一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one model: the same path walked again, with the accent on the manner of walking rather than on the path itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个模型展开：仍是同一条被反复行走的路，只是重心落在走的方式，而非路本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand ticking the same box on a list, moving before the eyes have read the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在清单上勾同一个格子，眼睛还没读到那一行，手已经动了。

branches.en: FIXED MANNER: the core sense describes doing a task in the established order, and the daily sense adds the calendar.
branches.cn: 固定方式：核心义指按既定次序做事，每日义再添上日历。

branches.en: USUAL CASE: what is done by habit becomes what generally happens, until it reads as a general rule.
branches.cn: 通常情形：按习惯做的事变成通常发生的事，最后读作通则。

branches.en: WITHOUT THOUGHT: the same path walked blindly turns the act into a reflex.
branches.cn: 不加思索：同一条路被盲目地走，动作就成了反射。

branches.en: SET PROCEDURE: an organised procedure applied to every case makes the act systematic.
branches.cn: 既定程序：有组织、覆盖每一例的程序使行为系统化。

branches.en: REGULAR RHYTHM AND CUSTOM: fixed intervals and unwritten institutional practice give the adverb its two public senses.
branches.cn: 固定节拍与惯例：固定间隔与不成文的机构做法给出副词的两种公共含义。

intro.en: The adverb is a transparent construction: a borrowed noun of habit plus a native manner suffix, so its parts can be read directly.
intro.cn: 这个副词是透明的构造：一个借入的「习惯」名词加上本族表方式的后缀，因此各部分可以直接读出。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer supplies the opened way and the road, the French layer the noun of habitual action, and English only supplies the adverb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层提供「被开出的路」与「道路」，法语层提供表惯常行为的名词，英语只提供副词词尾。

items.example: The root appears in English words about breaking: abrupt, bankrupt, interrupt.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在表示断裂的英语词里，如突然的、破产的、打断。

items.example: The noun meant any road, and the phrase joined it to a participle.
items.exampleCN: 这个词泛指任何道路，词组把它与一个分词连在一起。

items.meaning: a road or a chosen way
items.example: The courier chose the shortest route north.
items.exampleCN: 信使选了向北最短的路线。

items.structure: route plus a French noun suffix
items.example: The ward routine never varied.
items.exampleCN: 病房的固定流程从不变动。

items.meaning: in the usual order, as a matter of course
items.example: Staff routinely log every visit.
items.exampleCN: 员工按惯例记录每次探视。

items.meaning: to make something a fixed procedure
items.meaningCN: 使流程化；使固定成常规
items.example: Managers routinize what they cannot control.
items.exampleCN: 管理者把管不住的事变成固定流程。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a fixed procedure
items.example: Routinization cut errors but froze initiative.
items.exampleCN: 流程化减少了错误，却冻住了主动性。

items.example: A routineer distrusts any new step.
items.exampleCN: 墨守成规者对任何新步骤都不信任。

latinEntries.meaning: a broken or opened thing; the opened part in the phrase for an opened way
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被破开之物；表「被开出的路」的词组中指被开出的部分

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀后得到基础词，语义为「惯例、固定流程」
由基础词加表「使…化」的动词后缀构成，语义偏移为「使成为固定流程」
由上一动词再加表过程的名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「流程化」
由基础词加表「人」的后缀构成，语义偏移为「只按旧例办事的人」

definition_zh: n. 实况解说；评论；评注
definition_en: a spoken description of an event as it happens, or written notes explaining something
core_image: 球场直播里解说员的声音一直没停
scene: 球赛直播里，解说员的声音一直没停。 The commentary ran non-stop through the live match.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commentary 指实况解说；句意是球赛直播里，解说员的声音一直没停。

senses.title: A spoken description of an event
senses.definition: a broadcast description of a game or ceremony as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 对比赛或仪式进行中的广播描述
senses.example: His commentary made the dull match exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解说让乏味的比赛变得精彩。
senses.why: Radio and television gave the word this everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 广播与电视赋予这个词日常用法。

senses.title: Explanatory or critical notes
senses.definition: written notes explaining a text, or remarks on society
senses.definitionCN: 解释文本的书面注记，或对社会发表的议论
senses.example: The edition includes a scholarly commentary.
senses.exampleCN: 这个版本附有学术评注。
senses.why: Latin commentarius was a notebook of notes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 commentarius 是一本注记册。

intro.en: Commentary comes from a Latin word for a notebook of notes.
intro.cn: commentary 源自拉丁语「注记册」一词。

items.en: Commentum means a note or invention.
items.cn: commentum 意为注记或编造。

items.en: Commentarius means a notebook.
items.cn: commentarius 意为注记册。

items.en: Commentary first meant a set of notes.
items.cn: 十五世纪 commentary 首先指一组注记。

items.en: Radio made it a running description.
items.cn: 二十世纪广播使它成为连续解说。

items.en: Television keeps commentary live.
items.cn: 现代电视保持解说的现场性。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the comment- shape; the near-meaning group names description and critique.
note.cn: 形近组共享 comment- 词形；近义组列出描述与批评。

entries.definition: A single remark.
entries.definitionCN: 一条评论。

entries.definition: One who gives commentary.
entries.definitionCN: 解说员。

entries.definition: To praise.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞。

entries.definition: The act of narrating.
entries.definitionCN: 叙述。

entries.definition: A close examination.
entries.definitionCN: 分析。

entries.definition: A detailed judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 评论。

normalIntro.en: Commentary is a stream of comment, live or on the page.
normalIntro.cn: commentary 是一连串评论，或在现场，或在纸上。

normal.en: Commentarius was a notebook.
normal.cn: commentarius 是注记册。

normal.en: Commentary began as notes on a text.
normal.cn: commentary 起初是文本注记。

normal.en: On radio it became live description.
normal.cn: 在广播里它变成现场解说。

normal.en: A commentator gives commentary.
normal.cn: commentator 提供 commentary。

normal.en: A film can be social commentary.
normal.cn: 电影也可以是社会评论。

abstract.en: A voice over a moving picture.
abstract.cn: 画面之上的一把声音。

abstract.en: Notes in a book margin.
abstract.cn: 书页边上的注记。

abstract.en: A crowd explained as it cheers.
abstract.cn: 在欢呼中被讲解的人群。

examples.en: The commentary was broadcast in three languages.
examples.cn: 解说用三种语言播出。

examples.en: Her essay is a commentary on modern work.
examples.cn: 她的文章是对现代工作的评论。

examples.en: The book offers a commentary on each poem.
examples.cn: 这本书为每首诗提供评注。

dict_mnemonic.text: comment（注释）+ -ary（名词后缀）→ 成串的注释，即解说与评注。

root: 拉丁 commentum（注记）→ commentarius（注记册）→ 英语 commentary

sensesIntro.en: The same word explains a poem in a margin and a goal on television.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既解释书页边上的诗，也解释电视里的进球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice speaking over a live picture
core.cn: 核心意象：画面上方一把不停说话的声音

branches.en: A voice tracking a match.
branches.cn: 跟随比赛的一把声音。

branches.en: A parade described as it passes.
branches.cn: 边走边讲的游行。

branches.en: Notes beside a poem.
branches.cn: 诗旁的注记。

branches.en: A film read as social criticism.
branches.cn: 被读作社会批评的电影。

branches.en: Explanation, spoken or written, beside the event.
branches.cn: 在事件旁的解说，或说或写。

intro.en: Commentary is built from noting and telling; the list adds critique pieces.
intro.cn: commentary 由「注记」与「讲述」词素构成；下面列出批评词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin commentum is a note, narrare is to tell, and criticus is able to judge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 commentum 意为注记，narrare 意为讲述，criticus 意为能判断的。

definition_zh: 悲观主义者；总是预期最坏结果的人
definition_en: a person who expects the worst outcome, either as a philosophy or as a habit
core_image: 一桌人正在吃饭，有人已经先在心里把菜算成了不够
scene: 每回开新项目，他先数会出问题的地方，大家干脆叫他悲观主义者。 At every new project he counted what could go wrong, and the team called him a pessimist before the first week ended.
sceneCN: 这里 pessimist 指团队里的悲观者（第 2 个义项：惯于悲观的性格）；句意为每个新项目他都先数会出问题的地方，第一周还没过团队就这样叫他。

pos.zh: 悲观主义者；总是预期最坏结果的人

senses.title: Philosophical pessimist
senses.definition: one who holds that life holds more pain than good and that this cannot be repaired
senses.definitionCN: 认为生命中的苦多于好、且无法修补的人
senses.example: Schopenhauer is usually read as the philosophical pessimist.
senses.exampleCN: 叔本华通常被读作哲学上的悲观主义者。
senses.why: This sense is a position argued in books, not a mood on a given morning.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是书里论证的立场，不是某个早晨的心情。

senses.title: Habitual pessimist
senses.definition: a person whose first guess about any outcome is the bad one
senses.definitionCN: 对任何结果的第一猜测都是坏结果的人
senses.example: He is the office pessimist, and he is usually right.
senses.exampleCN: 他是办公室里的悲观者，而且通常猜对。
senses.why: Here the word describes a reflex, not a theory.
senses.whyCN: 这里描述的是条件反射，不是理论。

senses.title: Economic pessimist
senses.definition: one who expects markets to fall and hard times to last
senses.definitionCN: 预期市场下跌、艰难时期持续的人
senses.example: The economist was a pessimist about the housing market.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经济学家对住房市场持悲观看法。
senses.why: Forecasts make the word public: a view with dates and numbers attached.
senses.whyCN: 预测让这个词变得公开：一个带日期与数字的看法。

senses.title: Pessimist as realist
senses.definition: a person who calls his gloom a clear look at the facts
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的阴郁称为对事实的清醒审视的人
senses.example: Every pessimist claims he is simply a realist.
senses.exampleCN: 每个悲观者都说自己只是个现实主义者。
senses.why: The word is often a label the speaker rejects while using it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常是说话者一边用、一边拒绝的标签。

senses.title: Team pessimist
senses.definition: the member who lists the risks before anyone has chosen a name
senses.definitionCN: 在别人还没定名之前就先列出风险的那个人
senses.example: The team pessimist saved them from a costly launch.
senses.exampleCN: 团队里那个泼冷水的人让他们避免了一次代价高昂的上市。
senses.why: In groups the word can be a criticism or a quiet compliment.
senses.whyCN: 在群体里，这个词可以是批评，也可以是一句安静的称赞。

senses.title: Temperamental pessimist
senses.definition: a mood that expects loss before any evidence has arrived
senses.definitionCN: 证据还没出现就先预期损失的心情
senses.example: Her pessimist's mood lifted only on the last day.
senses.exampleCN: 她那悲观的心情直到最后一天才松开。
senses.why: The noun reaches for a temperament, which is older than any argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指向一种性情，它比任何论证都更早存在。

senses.title: Pessimist about people
senses.definition: one who doubts that people will act well without pressure
senses.definitionCN: 怀疑人在没有压力时就会好好行事的人
senses.example: The old judge was a pessimist about human nature.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老法官对人性的看法很悲观。
senses.why: This sense is about other people, not about one's own fortune.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎别人，而非自己的运气。

senses.title: Stock figure
senses.definition: the cartoon figure imagined to enjoy bad news
senses.definitionCN: 卡通里那个被想象成爱听坏消息的形象
senses.example: The pessimist of the cartoons is never invited to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 卡通里的悲观的家伙从来不在被邀请之列。
senses.why: The stereotype is a joke about the word, not a description of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个刻板印象是关于这个词的笑话，不是对它的描述。

intro.en: Pessimist comes from the Latin superlative for 'worst': the mind has already gone to the bottom of the scale.
intro.cn: pessimist 来自拉丁语表示「最坏」的最高级：心已经先走到了刻度最底。

items.en: Pessimus meant 'worst', the superlative of malus, 'bad'.
items.cn: pessimus 意为「最坏」，是 malus（坏）的最高级。

items.en: Malus supplied a whole family: malice, malign, malady.
items.cn: malus 提供了一整族词：malice、malign、malady。

items.en: Pessimism was coined in the eighteenth century as the opposite of optimism.
items.cn: pessimism 在十八世纪被造出，作为 optimism 的反面。

items.en: The word grew out of the argument over whether this is the best of all possible worlds.
items.cn: 这个词从「这是否是可能世界中最好的一个」的争论里长出来。

items.en: Schopenhauer and others turned the label into a system, and the person into a pessimist.
items.cn: 叔本华等人把这个标签变成体系，也把人变成 pessimist。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pessimism family; the near-meaning group separates the cynic, the defeatist and the doomsayer.
note.cn: 形近组是 pessimism 词族；近义组把「愤世者」「失败主义者」与「末日预言者」分开。

entries.definition: the belief that the bad outweighs the good.
entries.definitionCN: 认为坏多于好的信念。

entries.definition: expecting the worse outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 预期更坏结果的。

entries.definition: in a way that expects the worst.
entries.definitionCN: 以预期最坏的方式。

entries.definition: people who expect the worst.
entries.definitionCN: 期待最坏结果的人们。

entries.definition: one who trusts no one's motives.
entries.definitionCN: 不信任任何人动机的人。

entries.definition: one who expects to lose and acts on it.
entries.definitionCN: 预期失败并据此行事的人。

entries.definition: one who announces coming disaster.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告灾难将至的人。

entries.definition: one who exaggerates danger.
entries.definitionCN: 夸大危险的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a person who has already counted the plates and found them short.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「有人已经数过盘子、先算出不够」的画面。

normal.en: Pessimist holds pessimus, Latin for worst: the mind starts at the bottom of the scale.
normal.cn: pessimist 里藏着 pessimus（拉丁语的「最坏」）：心从刻度最底开始。

normal.en: Think of a dinner guest who counts the plates before the food arrives.
normal.cn: 想象一位客人，菜还没上就先数盘子。

normal.en: Pes-si-MIST: the stress sits on mis, and the mist is already closing in.
normal.cn: pes-si-MIST：重音落在 mis 上，雾也已经合拢。

normal.en: Say PESS-uh-mist; the first syllable already sounds like a sigh.
normal.cn: 读成 PESS-uh-mist，第一个音节已经像一声叹气。

normal.en: Pair it with optimist: the two words are the same machine, running in opposite directions.
normal.cn: 把它和 optimist 配对：两个词是同一台机器，朝相反方向转。

abstract.en: A pessimist is not always wrong; he is a person whose guesses are graded on a steeper curve.
abstract.cn: 悲观者不总是错的；他只是把猜测放在一条更陡的曲线上评分。

abstract.en: The word can name a philosophy, a temperament or an office role, and only the first one has arguments.
abstract.cn: 这个词可以命名一种哲学、一种性情或一个办公室角色，其中只有第一种带论证。

abstract.en: Every pessimist keeps a small hope somewhere, which is why the word is never quite stable.
abstract.cn: 每个悲观者心里都留着一点希望，所以这个词从不十分稳定。

examples.en: The team called him a pessimist before the first week ended.
examples.cn: 第一周还没过，团队就叫他悲观主义者。

examples.en: The economist was a pessimist about the housing market.
examples.cn: 这位经济学家对住房市场持悲观看法。

examples.en: Every pessimist claims he is simply a realist.
examples.cn: 每个悲观者都说自己只是个现实主义者。

dict_mnemonic.text: pessim（最坏）+ ist（人）：总把结果往最坏处算的人，就是「悲观主义者」。

root: 拉丁语 pessimus（最坏的），malus（坏）的最高级，加 -ist（表人后缀）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses move from a system in a book to a face at a party: a philosophy, a habit, a forecast, a claim, a team role, a temperament, a view of people and a cartoon.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从书里的体系走到聚会上的那张脸：哲学、习惯、预测、自我辩解、团队角色、性情、对人性的看法与一个卡通形象。

core.en: A SCALE THAT STARTS AT THE BOTTOM
core.cn: 从最底端开始的刻度

chain: THE MIND GOES TO THE WORST

branches.en: A position argued in books.
branches.cn: 书里论证过的立场。

branches.en: A reflex and a temperament, both older than argument.
branches.cn: 条件反射与性情，都比论证更早。

branches.en: A forecast with dates and a role inside a team.
branches.cn: 带日期的预测与团队里的角色。

branches.en: The claim to realism and the verdict on other people.
branches.cn: 自称现实与对他人的判断。

branches.en: The cartoon figure that the word now drags behind it.
branches.cn: 这个词如今拖在身后的卡通形象。

intro.en: The pessimism family is a small seesaw: pessimism at one end, optimism at the other, and the same -ism and -ist endings on both.
intro.cn: pessimism 词族是一副小跷跷板：一端是 pessimism，一端是 optimism，两边用的都是 -ism 与 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Latin pessimus supplies 'worst' and malus supplies 'bad'; the endings -ism and -ist turn a judgement into a system and a person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pessimus 提供「最坏」，malus 提供「坏」；词尾 -ism 与 -ist 把一个判断变成体系与人。

definition_zh: 驴叫；粗厉地叫；刺耳地说或吹奏
definition_en: to make the loud harsh cry of a donkey; to utter or play harshly
core_image: 驴昂起头，喉咙一收一放，发出拖长而刺耳的「昂——昂——」
scene: 清晨的农场还睡着眼。 A donkey's bray tore through the quiet of the farmyard.
sceneCN: 这里 bray 是「驴叫」（第 1 个义项：驴的粗厉叫声，此处作名词）；句意是一声驴叫划破了农院的清晨。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「驴叫；粗厉声」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「发粗厉声者」

senses.title: The donkey's loud harsh cry
senses.definition: the loud, broken cry characteristic of a donkey, as verb or noun
senses.definitionCN: 驴特有的响亮断续叫声，作动词或名词
senses.example: The donkey brayed at the rising sun.
senses.exampleCN: 驴对着朝阳叫了起来。
senses.why: The word began as pure sound imitation of the animal's two-tone hee-haw.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初就是对驴「两声部」叫声的纯粹拟声。

senses.title: To laugh loudly and harshly
senses.definition: to laugh in a loud, unpleasant, donkey-like way
senses.definitionCN: 以响亮难听、似驴的方式大笑
senses.example: He brayed with laughter at his own joke.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己讲的笑话粗声大笑。
senses.why: A human sound resembling the donkey's cry borrows the animal's name for it.
senses.whyCN: 人声若酷似驴叫，便借用驴叫之名。

senses.title: To speak in a loud harsh voice
senses.definition: to talk loudly and unpleasantly, as if through a cracked horn
senses.definitionCN: 大声而难听地说话，仿佛隔着破喇叭
senses.example: The sergeant brayed out the orders.
senses.exampleCN: 中士粗声吼出命令。
senses.why: The harshness of the cry transfers to any harsh human voice.
senses.whyCN: 叫声的粗厉转移到一切粗厉的人声上。

senses.title: To play an instrument harshly
senses.definition: to produce a loud harsh sound on a horn or trumpet
senses.definitionCN: 在号或小号上发出响而刺耳的声音
senses.example: The old gramophone brayed out a march.
senses.exampleCN: 老式留声机刺耳地放出一支进行曲。
senses.why: Instruments crack and buzz exactly as a donkey's throat does.
senses.whyCN: 乐器劈裂嗡鸣的音色恰似驴的喉音。

senses.title: To trumpet foolishly, of a person
senses.definition: to talk in a self-important but foolish way
senses.definitionCN: 以自以为重要实则愚蠢的方式高声谈论
senses.example: Politicians brayed about reforms they never made.
senses.exampleCN: 政客们咋咋呼呼地谈着从未实行的改革。
senses.why: Since the ass stands for foolishness, its voice marks foolish speech.
senses.whyCN: 驴既象征愚笨，其叫声便标记愚蠢的言谈。

senses.title: A harsh crushing sound, as of machinery
senses.definition: a loud grating noise of engines or brakes
senses.definitionCN: 发动机或刹车发出的刺耳摩擦声
senses.example: The train brayed to a stop.
senses.exampleCN: 火车一路刺耳地刹停。
senses.why: Metal grinding resembles the broken, grinding donkey cry.
senses.whyCN: 金属摩擦声与断续刺耳的驴叫如出一辙。

senses.title: To pound and crush, as in mortar
senses.definition: in older use, to pound or grind substances in a mortar
senses.definitionCN: 旧义指在研钵中捣碎或研磨物料
senses.example: Apothecaries brayed roots into powder.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师把草根捣成粉末。
senses.why: A different Middle English word of the same shape meant to pound; the two mingled in spelling.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语另有一个同形词意为捣碎，两词在拼写上混流。

senses.title: To beat with a rod, in old law
senses.definition: in medieval law, to punish by beating or flogging
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪法律用语：以鞭笞为惩罚
senses.example: Old statutes ordered offenders to be brayed at the post.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法令规定罪人在刑柱前受笞。
senses.why: The pounding sense extended to pounding a person in punishment.
senses.whyCN: 「捣碎」义延伸到把人「捣打」以示惩罚。

intro.en: Bray is an imitative Middle English word for the donkey's cry, with a separate Middle Dutch homophone meaning to pound.
intro.cn: bray 是中古英语对驴叫的拟声词；另有一个同形的中古荷兰语词，意为捣碎。

items.en: The donkey cry word arose by imitation of the animal's two-tone call; no deeper root is traceable.
items.cn: 驴叫义源于对动物双音叫声的模仿，无法追溯更深的词根。

items.en: Breien and brayen appear in early texts for the braying of asses.
items.cn: 早期文献以 breien、brayen 记录驴叫。

items.en: A separate Middle Dutch brayen meant to pound or crush, borrowed into English trades.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语另有 brayen，意为捣碎，随行话进入英语。

items.en: The pounding word passed into legal use for flogging as a punishment.
items.cn: 捣碎义进入法律用语，指杖笞之刑。

items.en: Shakespeare's Midsummer Night's Dream fixed the ass's bray in the literary canon.
items.cn: 莎剧《仲夏夜之梦》把驴叫定格于文学正典。

items.en: Modern use favors the animal cry and its figurative harsh voices and laughs.
items.cn: 现代用法以驴叫及其比喻性的粗厉人声、笑声为主。

note.en: Bray's sound twins are many, and only one is related; its near group is the family of animal cries.
note.cn: bray 的同音词不少，但仅一词同源；近义组是各类动物叫声。

entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰语「山坡」；与 bray 同音，词源不同

entries.definition: the deep roar of a bull

entries.definition: the cry of a sheep or goat

entries.definition: the sharp cry of a hen; also harsh laughter

abstract.en: The sound of something honest but unlovely.

examples.en: The candidate brayed promises through a faulty loudspeaker.
examples.cn: 候选人隔着失灵的扩音器大声嚷着种种许诺。

examples.en: Her bray of laughter turned every head in the café.
examples.cn: 她那声粗厉的大笑让咖啡馆里所有人都回过头来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不～累」——驴叫拖长音「昂～」，一问一答像喊「不～累～」：拖着长音的粗嗓门就是 bray。

sensesIntro.en: The donkey's cry is the seed; from it grow harsh laughter, harsh speech, harsh instruments, and even the old trades of pounding and flogging.
sensesIntro.cn: 驴叫是种子；由此长出粗厉的笑、粗厉的话、刺耳的乐器声，乃至捣碎与杖笞的旧业。

definition_zh: 可重复性；可复现性；再现性；复现能力
definition_en: the ability of a result or experiment to be obtained again by the same or another researcher
core_image: 两间实验室各摆一套相同的仪器，两张记录纸上画着几乎一样的曲线
scene: 两间实验室各摆着一套相同的仪器，两位技术员按同一份步骤各做一遍，两张记录纸上画出几乎一样的曲线。 The reproducibility of the assay was checked in two labs before the paper was submitted.
sceneCN: 这里指他人按同样条件能再次得到相同结果的程度（第 1 个义项：结果能被再次得到的性质）；句意为论文投稿之前，这项检测的可重复性已在两间实验室核对过。图中可辨识物件：两套仪器、记录纸、曲线、操作步骤单。

pos.zh: 可重复性；可复现性；再现性

senses.title: The result can be obtained again
senses.definition: the degree to which the same result can be obtained again under the same conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在相同条件下能再次得到同一结果的程度
senses.example: The reproducibility of the assay was checked in two labs before the paper was submitted.
senses.exampleCN: 论文投稿之前，这项检测的可重复性已在两间实验室核对过。
senses.why: Reproduce joins re- again to produce, so the noun names the ability to bring the same result forth again.
senses.whyCN: 动词把表示「再次」的前缀加到「产出」之上，名词便命名「再次产出同一结果」的能力。

senses.title: The experiment can be repeated
senses.definition: the quality of an experiment whose whole procedure can be followed again by another team
senses.definitionCN: 整套步骤能被另一个团队照着再做一遍的性质
senses.example: Careful reproducibility requires a protocol that another team can follow.
senses.exampleCN: 要做到可重复，研究方案必须详细到另一个团队能照着做。
senses.why: The word covers the procedure as well as the number, because a result cannot return without the steps.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既覆盖步骤也覆盖数值，因为没有步骤，结果就回不来。

senses.title: The crisis of missing repeats
senses.definition: the public concern that many published findings cannot be repeated
senses.definitionCN: 许多已发表发现无法被重复所引发的公共担忧
senses.example: The conference was called to discuss the reproducibility crisis in psychology.
senses.exampleCN: 这次会议专门讨论心理学中的可重复性危机。
senses.why: When many claims fail the test, the quality becomes the name of a field-wide problem.
senses.whyCN: 当许多主张都过不了这道检验，这种性质就成了整个领域的问题之名。

senses.title: The stability of an instrument
senses.definition: the consistency of readings given by an instrument on repeated measurement
senses.definitionCN: 仪器反复测量同一对象时读数的稳定性
senses.example: The reproducibility of the balance was tested with the same standard block.
senses.exampleCN: 天平的再现性用同一块标准砝码作了检验。
senses.why: Instruments also produce again, and their reproducibility is a property of the machine.
senses.whyCN: 仪器也会再次产出，它的再现性是机器本身的属性。

senses.title: Batch-to-batch repeatability
senses.titleCN: 批与批之间的再现精度
senses.definition: the consistency of a manufactured product from one batch to the next
senses.definitionCN: 制成品从一批到下一批的一致性
senses.example: The plant records the reproducibility of each batch within narrow limits.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把每一批的再现精度都记录在很窄的范围内。
senses.why: Manufacturing asks the same question as science: can the same thing be made again?
senses.whyCN: 制造业问的与科学同一个问题：同样的东西还能再做一次吗？

senses.title: The same code gives the same output
senses.titleCN: 同一代码给出同一输出
senses.definition: the ability to rerun an analysis from the same data and code and obtain the same output
senses.definitionCN: 用同一数据与代码重跑分析、得到同一输出的能力
senses.example: Computational reproducibility means the same code gives the same output.
senses.exampleCN: 计算可复现性意味着同一份代码给出同一份输出。
senses.why: Computers brought a new kind of repeatability, where the steps are files rather than hands.
senses.whyCN: 计算机带来一种新的可重复性，步骤是文件而不是人手。

senses.title: The standard a journal demands
senses.titleCN: 期刊要求的可重复标准
senses.definition: a formal requirement that authors provide enough material for others to repeat the work
senses.definitionCN: 要求作者提供足够材料、使他人能重复这项工作的正式规定
senses.example: The journal now enforces a reproducibility standard for its papers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家期刊现在对论文执行可重复性标准。
senses.why: Once the quality is valued, it becomes a rule that can be checked.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质一旦被看重，就变成可以核查的规则。

senses.title: The failure to repeat
senses.definition: the absence of reproducibility, when a second attempt does not produce the same result
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏可重复性，即第二次尝试没有得到同一结果
senses.example: The lack of reproducibility in the earlier study delayed the drug's approval.
senses.exampleCN: 早先研究缺乏可重复性，拖延了这种药的批准。
senses.why: The noun can name the failure as well as the virtue, because both are measured by the second attempt.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能命名美德也能命名失败，因为两者都由第二次尝试来衡量。

intro.en: Reproducibility is reproduce plus -ible plus -ity, a Latin-derived stack. Reproduce comes from re- again and Latin producere, to lead forward. The source is clear; the date of the noun's first record is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词由「产出」动词先加表示「能够」的后缀，再加表示「性质」的后缀构成。该动词来自表示「再次」的前缀与拉丁 producere「向前引出」。词源清楚，名词最早记录的年代不确定。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead, and it stands inside producere as the moving element.
items.cn: ducere 意为引导，作为「带动」的成分藏在 producere 里。

items.en: Producere joined pro- forward to ducere, meaning to lead or bring forth.
items.cn: producere 把意为「向前」的前缀加到 ducere 上，意为引出、带出。

items.en: The prefix re- adds the sense of doing it once more, giving reproduce.
items.cn: 表示「再次」的前缀加上「再做一次」的意思，构成「再次产出」的动词。

items.en: Latin -ibilis means able to be, so reproducible means able to be produced again.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -ibilis 意为「能够被……」，因此「可复现的」指能够被再次产出。

items.en: Latin -itas turns the adjective into the name of the quality.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -itas 把形容词变成这种性质的名称。

items.en: Twentieth-century science made reproducibility a technical demand; the phrase reproducibility crisis is recent, and its first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 二十世纪科学使这个词成为技术要求；「可重复性危机」这一说法出现较晚，起始年代不确定。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like reproducibility; the second names qualities it is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「本词」相近；第二组是常与它混淆的性质。

entries.definition: To produce again, or to make offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 再次产出，或繁殖后代。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that can be produced again.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够被再次产出的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a repeatable way.
entries.definitionCN: 以可重复的方式做某事的副词。

entries.definition: The act of copying or the process of producing offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 复制行为或繁殖过程。

entries.definition: Relating to producing offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 与繁殖后代有关的。

entries.definition: The chance of getting the same result when one person repeats the same measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个人重复同一测量时得到同一结果的机会。

entries.definition: The chance that another team can repeat a study and find the same result.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个团队重复研究并得到同一结果的机会。

entries.definition: Consistency of measurement over time, a narrower quality.
entries.definitionCN: 测量随时间的稳定性，是一种更窄的性质。

entries.definition: Agreement among repeated results, without saying they are right.
entries.definitionCN: 多次结果彼此一致，但不说明它们是对的。

entries.definition: The tendency to stay the same rather than to be produced again.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于保持不变，而不是再次被产出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin produce word, the real -ible and -ity stack and real science terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「产出」词、真实的「能够」与「性质」两个后缀叠加，以及真实科学术语。

normal.en: Reproducibility is reproduce plus -ible plus -ity: the ability to be produced again.
normal.cn: reproducibility 是 reproduce 加 -ible 再加 -ity：能够被再次产出的能力。

normal.en: Producere meant to lead forward, and re- adds a second leading.
normal.cn: producere 意为向前引出，re- 又加上第二次引出。

normal.en: Fixed phrases include reproducibility crisis, reproducibility standard and computational reproducibility.
normal.cn: 固定说法有可重复性危机、可重复性标准与计算可复现性。

normal.en: Two labs, one protocol and nearly one curve: that is reproducibility in a picture.
normal.cn: 两间实验室、一份步骤、几乎一条曲线：这就是可重复性的画面。

normal.en: A journal that enforces a reproducibility standard is asking for the steps, not just the answer.
normal.cn: 执行可重复性标准的期刊，要的是步骤，不只是答案。

abstract.en: Reproducibility is the promise that the second try will not tell a different story.
abstract.cn: 可重复性是那个承诺：第二次尝试不会讲出另一个故事。

abstract.en: A result that no one can produce again is a rumour with numbers attached.
abstract.cn: 没人能再次产出的结果，只是带着数字的传闻。

abstract.en: The word measures science against its own claim to be public knowledge.
abstract.cn: 这个词用科学自称的「公共知识」来衡量科学本身。

examples.en: The team improved the reproducibility by writing down every step.
examples.cn: 团队把每一步都写下来，从而提高了可重复性。

examples.en: Reproducibility is now a condition for funding in some fields.
examples.cn: 在某些领域，可重复性如今是获得资助的条件。

examples.en: The report ranked the studies by their reproducibility.
examples.cn: 报告按可重复性对这些研究作了排序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「再次产出的能力」——同一结果还能再做出来：可重复性

root: 这个词由意为「再次」的前缀、意为「产出」的词根与表示「能够」「性质」的两个后缀叠加构成。词根源自拉丁 producere「向前引出」（前缀意为「向前」加词根意为「引导」）。二十世纪科学使它成为技术术语，二〇一〇年代前后出现「可重复性危机」说法；词源清楚，最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one second attempt: the same result again, the repeatable experiment, the crisis of failed repeats, instrument stability, batch consistency, computational replay, a journal standard, and the failure to repeat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「第二次尝试」：再次得到同一结果、可重复的实验、复现失败的危机、仪器稳定性、批次一致性、计算重跑、期刊标准，以及无法重复的失败。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two labs, one protocol, and two record sheets carrying almost the same curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：两间实验室、一份步骤，两张记录纸上画着几乎一样的曲线。

branches.en: THE RESULT AND THE PROCEDURE: the number returns, and the steps make its return possible.
branches.cn: 结果与步骤：数值回来了，而步骤使这个回来成为可能。

branches.en: THE CRISIS: when many results fail to return, the quality becomes a public problem.
branches.cn: 危机：当许多结果回不来，这种性质就成了公共问题。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND THE FACTORY: instruments and batches must give the same reading or the same product.
branches.cn: 仪器与工厂：仪器与批次必须给出同一读数或同一产品。

branches.en: THE CODE AND THE RULE: a replay from files, and a journal that demands the files.
branches.cn: 代码与规则：从文件重跑，以及要求交出文件的期刊。

branches.en: THE FAILURE: the same word names the absence of the quality.
branches.cn: 失败：同一个词也命名这种性质的缺失。

intro.en: Reproducibility is a three-part Latin stack on an English verb: re- plus produce plus -ible plus -ity.
intro.cn: reproducibility 是在英语动词上叠三层拉丁成分：re- 加 produce 再加 -ible 与 -ity。

latinIntro.en: Latin producere, ducere and the endings -ibilis and -itas supply the structure of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 producere、ducere 与后缀 -ibilis、-itas 提供这个词的结构。

items.example: The prefix asks for a second producing.

items.example: The verb names the act of bringing back a result.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把结果再次带回来的行为。

items.example: It builds reproducible from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成表示「可复现的」形容词。

items.example: It builds reproducibility from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它由形容词构成表示「可重复性」的名词。

items.example: The adjective describes the result or the procedure.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述结果或步骤。

items.example: The adverb marks how the work was done.
items.exampleCN: 副词标出工作是怎样做的。
