definition_zh: 可以说；有理由认为；可论证地；大概可以算作
definition_en: used to present a claim as one that can be supported by argument or reason, while leaving room for disagreement
core_image: 一栋楼的评价被写在稿纸上，定论后面留着一小块空白，像给反驳留了座位
scene: 评审席上两个人对同一栋楼给出不同评价，评论家在稿子里写下一句带保留的定论。 She is arguably the finest translator of her generation.
sceneCN: 这里指给最高级的判断留出余地（第 2 个义项：给最高级留余地）；句意为她大概可以算作她那一代最出色的译者。场景要点：两张不同评价的评审单、稿纸上带保留的句子、定论后留出的空白。

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁动词经法语构成，义为「论证、争辩」
由论证动词加表示「可……的」形容词词尾构成，义为「可论证的、有争议的」
由同一词源加表示行为结果的名词尾构成，义为「论证、争论」
由论证名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「好争辩的、论证性的」
由论证动词加表示行为的名词尾构成，义为「论证过程」

senses.title: One can reasonably argue that
senses.definition: presents a statement as defensible on the evidence available, without claiming that it is settled
senses.definitionCN: 把一项说法呈现为依现有证据站得住，但不声称它已成定论
senses.example: Arguably, the harbour scheme did more harm than good.
senses.exampleCN: 可以说，那个港口方案弊大于利。
senses.why: Arguere means to make clear by argument, so the word offers a case rather than a verdict.
senses.whyCN: arguere 意为「用论证说清楚」，因此这个词给出的是一个理由，而不是一个判决。

senses.title: Softening a superlative
senses.definition: placed before the best, worst or most to mark a judgement that a reasonable person could dispute
senses.definitionCN: 放在「最好的、最坏的、最……」之前，标明这是一个旁人可以有理由反对的判断
senses.example: She is arguably the finest translator of her generation.
senses.exampleCN: 她大概可以算作她那一代最出色的译者。
senses.why: A superlative sounds absolute, and the adverb reopens the space that the superlative had closed.
senses.whyCN: 最高级听起来绝对，这个副词把最高级关上的那扇门又推开一条缝。

senses.title: Hedging in academic writing
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的谨慎断言
senses.definition: used to avoid claiming proof where the evidence supports only a case
senses.definitionCN: 在证据只能支持一种理由、不足以构成证明时，避免声称已经证明
senses.example: Arguably, the two variables are linked through a third factor.
senses.exampleCN: 可以说，这两个变量是通过第三个因素联系起来的。
senses.why: Academic style needs a way to advance a thesis while leaving it open to challenge, and this is that way.
senses.whyCN: 学术文体需要一种既能提出论点、又允许被质疑的说法，这个词就是那种说法。

senses.title: A concession to the other side
senses.definition: used to grant that an opposing reading has force before answering it
senses.definitionCN: 在回应之前先承认对立的读法确有分量
senses.example: Arguably, the earlier study was right about the direction of change.
senses.exampleCN: 可以说，早先那项研究在变化方向上是对的。
senses.why: Granting a point is itself an argumentative move, and the word makes the grant without surrender.
senses.whyCN: 承认一点本身就是一种论证动作，这个词让承认不至于变成投降。

senses.title: Framing a case in debate
senses.definition: opens a position that the speaker intends to support with reasons
senses.definitionCN: 开启一个说话人打算用理由去支持的立场
senses.example: Arguably, the burden of proof lies with the applicant.
senses.exampleCN: 可以说，举证责任在申请人一方。
senses.why: Debate needs an opening that invites reasons, and the word signals that reasons are coming.
senses.whyCN: 辩论需要一个邀请理由进场的开场，这个词就提示理由随后就到。

senses.title: Questioning a claim in reply
senses.definition: in reply, often stressed, hints that the claim is doubtful rather than granting it
senses.definitionCN: 在应答中常带重音，暗示该说法可疑，而不是予以认可
senses.example: Arguably so, but the figures do not show it.
senses.exampleCN: 可以说确实如此，但数字并不支持。
senses.why: The same word can grant and doubt, and stress is what turns the grant into a question.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既能认可也能怀疑，重音就是把认可变成疑问的那一下。

senses.title: Provable in principle
senses.definition: the literal sense: capable of being supported by argument, whether or not anyone has yet done so
senses.definitionCN: 字面义：能够被论证支持，无论是否已有人论证过
senses.example: The result is arguably true for any finite sample.
senses.exampleCN: 这一结果对任何有限样本都可论证为真。
senses.why: The adverb is built on arguable, and arguable means open to argument, not merely likely.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由「可论证的」这一形容词构成，而该形容词指「可供论证」，并不等于「很可能」。

senses.title: The reviewer's evaluative tone
senses.titleCN: 评论文字中的评价语气
senses.definition: the critic's way of giving a firm opinion while leaving the formal claim unasserted
senses.definitionCN: 评论者给出明确看法、却不把话说成事实的方式
senses.example: It is arguably the most important building of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 它大概可以算作这十年里最重要的一座建筑。
senses.why: Reviewing lives on judgements that cannot be proved, so it needs a form of words that sounds decided but stays open.
senses.whyCN: 评论靠的是无法证明的判断，因此它需要一种听上去已定、实则留口的措辞。

senses.title: Not the same as probably
senses.definition: the word claims that a case can be made, not that the event is likely
senses.definitionCN: 这个词声称的是「能立论」，而不是「事情很可能发生」
senses.example: Arguably does not mean probably; it means a case can be made.
senses.exampleCN: 「可以说」并不是「很可能」，它的意思是能够给出理由。
senses.why: The word is built on arguable, which concerns reasons rather than chances, so the probability reading loses its whole point.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在「可论证的」这一形容词之上，而可论证关心的是理由而不是机会，因此读成概率就丢了全部要点。

intro.en: Arguably is arguable plus -ly, from argue, which comes from Latin arguere, to make clear, prove or accuse, through Old French arguer. The English hedging use is recent: the word offers a case, not a probability.
intro.cn: arguably 是 arguable 加 -ly，源自 argue；argue 经古法语 arguer 来自拉丁语 arguere「使清楚、证明、指控」。英语里这种留余地的用法出现较晚：它给出的是一个理由，而不是一个概率。

items.en: The verb meant to make clear, demonstrate or prove, and also to accuse or bring a charge.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使清楚、演示、证明，也指指控、提出罪状。

items.en: French narrowed the word towards reasoning and pleading in a dispute.
items.cn: 法语把这个词收窄到争议中的推理与申辩。

items.en: English kept both faces: setting out reasons, and quarrelling.
items.cn: 英语把两副面孔都留下了：摆出理由，以及争吵。

items.en: The adjective meant open to argument, and later also disputable.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为可供论证，后来也指有争议。

items.en: The hedge became common in journalism and scholarship in the twentieth century; the exact date of that shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 这种弱化用法在二十世纪的新闻与学术写作中变得常见；这一转变的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Reviewers and analysts now use it to sound decided without making a claim they would have to defend as fact.
items.cn: 评论者与分析者现在用它显得有定见，又不至于把话说成必须当作事实来辩护。

note.en: The first group shares the arguing stem; the second holds the hedges it is most often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组共享「论证」词干；第二组是常与它混淆的几种留余地说法。

entries.definition: To give reasons for a position, or to disagree noisily.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某立场给出理由，也指大声争执。

entries.definition: Open to argument, and in another use, doubtful.
entries.definitionCN: 指可供论证，另一用法指可疑。

entries.definition: A set of reasons, and also a quarrel.
entries.definitionCN: 指一组理由，也指争吵。

entries.definition: Given to arguing, or relating to argument as a form.
entries.definitionCN: 指好争辩的，或与论证形式有关的。

entries.definition: The systematic construction of arguments.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统地构造论证。

entries.definition: Marks what may reasonably be assumed from what is known.
entries.definitionCN: 标记依已知情况可合理假定的事。

entries.definition: Marks what can be imagined as possible, with no claim of support.
entries.definitionCN: 标记可以想象为可能的事，不声称有依据。

entries.definition: Reports what is said to be so, often with doubt attached.
entries.definitionCN: 转述据说如此，常带怀疑。

entries.definition: The plain marker of possibility, about likelihood rather than argument.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的可能标记，谈的是概率而非论证。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin verb of proving, the real argument family, and the hedging habit of reviewers.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语「证明」的动词、真实的论证词族，以及评论者留余地的习惯。

normal.en: Arguere is to make clear by argument, so arguably offers clarity that is still open to challenge.
normal.cn: 拉丁语里那个表示「用论证说清」的动词，给的是仍可被质疑的清楚。

normal.en: Argue, argument, arguable and arguably are one family, one root, four jobs.
normal.cn: 论证、论证性、可论证、可以说，四者同出一根，四份差事。

normal.en: Put it before a superlative and the absolute claim grows a door.
normal.cn: 把它放在最高级前面，绝对的说法就多了一扇门。

normal.en: In a seminar, arguably is the polite way to say here is my case, now test it.
normal.cn: 在研讨课上，「可以说」是「这是我的理由，请来检验」的礼貌说法。

normal.en: It does not measure probability: it measures whether reasons exist.
normal.cn: 它衡量的不是概率，而是有没有理由。

abstract.en: A claim that cannot be wrong is not an argument; arguably keeps the claim exposed on purpose.
abstract.cn: 不会错的主张不是论证；这个词故意让主张保持暴露。

abstract.en: The word is a door left ajar in a sentence that would otherwise be shut.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一句本已关上、却被留了一条缝的话。

abstract.en: Authority says it is so; arguably says here is why it might be so.
abstract.cn: 权威说事情就是这样；这个词说，这是它可能如此的理由。

examples.en: Arguably, the second design is the safer of the two.
examples.cn: 可以说，第二个设计是两者中更安全的一个。

examples.en: He is arguably the most influential critic writing today.
examples.cn: 他大概可以算作当今最有影响力的评论家。

examples.en: The delay was arguably caused by the change in specification.
examples.cn: 可以说，延期是由规格变更造成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿格优厄布利」——他也能讲出一套理由，但话还留着余地：可以说

root: 拉丁语 arguere「使清楚、证明、指控」→ 古法语 arguer → 英语 argue → arguable，再加副词词尾构成。直接来源清楚；作弱化断言的用法为二十世纪发展，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses vary the strength and target of the hedge: a defensible claim, a softened superlative, academic caution, a concession, a debate opening, a doubting reply, the literal sense of being arguable, the reviewer's tone, and the line between a case and a probability.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项改变的是留余地的力度与对象：站得住的主张、被软化的最高级、学术上的谨慎、对对方的让步、辩论开场、带疑的应答、字面上的「可论证」、评论者的语气，以及「能立论」与「很可能」的分界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a verdict written on a page, with a small blank left beside it where a challenge may sit.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸页上写下的一句定论，旁边留着一小块空白，给反驳留着座位。

branches.en: THE DEFENSIBLE CLAIM: reasons can be given, whether or not anyone has given them yet.
branches.cn: 站得住的主张：理由给得出，至于是否已给出则不论。

branches.en: THE SOFTENED VERDICT: a superlative reopened, a review that sounds decided but stays open.
branches.cn: 被软化的定论：最高级被重新推开，评论听来已定却仍留口。

branches.en: THE ACADEMIC AND DEBATE HEDGE: caution in a paper, an opening that invites reasons.
branches.cn: 学术与辩论中的留余地：论文里的谨慎，辩论里邀请理由进场的开场。

branches.en: THE CONCESSION: the other side is granted its force before the answer comes.
branches.cn: 让步：在回应之前，先承认对方那一面确有分量。

branches.en: THE DOUBT AND THE LIMIT: a stressed reply that questions, and the refusal to mean probably.
branches.cn: 疑问与界限：带重音的应答表示怀疑，以及它并不等于「很可能」。

intro.en: Arguably is a Latin verb of proving, filtered through French, wearing an English adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: arguably 是一个经法语过滤的拉丁「证明」动词，套着英语的形容词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies arguere and argumentum; Old French supplies arguer, and English builds argue, arguable and arguably on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 arguere 与 argumentum；古法语提供了 arguer，英语在同一词干上造出 argue、arguable 与 arguably。

items.example: The verb carries both proving and accusing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时带着「证明」与「指控」。

items.meaning: a proof, an argument, a subject
items.example: The noun names what the verb produces.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指动词所产出之物。

items.example: French carried the word into English use.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个词带入英语用法。

items.example: English keeps the reasoned and the quarrelsome sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼留「讲理」与「争吵」两义。

items.example: The suffix makes a claim that reasons can reach it.
items.exampleCN: 词尾造出一个「理由够得着」的说法。

items.example: It turns the verb into a possibility.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成一种可能性。

items.example: It makes the hedge adverb from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它由形容词构成这个留余地的副词。

items.example: It forms argument, the thing produced.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 argument，即产出之物。

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁动词经法语构成，义为「论证、争辩」
由论证动词加「可……的」形容词词尾构成，义为「可论证的」
由同一词源加表示行为结果的名词尾构成，义为「论证」
由论证名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「好争辩的」
由论证动词加表示行为的名词尾构成，义为「论证过程」

definition_zh: 化学反应；物质相互转化为新物质的过程
definition_en: a process in which substances change into different substances by rearranging their atoms
core_image: 烧杯里一蓝一绿两种溶液相遇，蓝色迅速褪去，气泡沿杯壁一串串往上爬
scene: 演示台上，学生把两种溶液倒进同一只烧杯，蓝色立即褪成浅绿，气泡顺着杯壁上浮，老师说 That colour change is proof that a chemical reaction has already begun.
sceneCN: 这里 chemical reaction 指「物质转变成新物质的过程」，取第 1 个义项（反应本身）；句意为这个颜色变化证明化学反应已经开始。图中可辨识物件：烧杯、气泡、滴管、实验记录板。

pos.zh: 化学反应（可数，复数 chemical reactions）

collocations.phrase: chemical reaction between A and B
collocations.zh: 甲与乙之间的化学反应

senses.title: Substances becoming new substances
senses.definition: a process in which atoms regroup so that the starting materials become different materials
senses.definitionCN: 原子重新组合，使原来的物质变成不同物质的过程
senses.example: Baking soda and vinegar give a familiar chemical reaction at home.
senses.exampleCN: 小苏打与醋在家里就能做出一个熟悉的化学反应。
senses.why: Reaction here means the mutual action of two substances, so the phrase names what happens when they act on each other.
senses.whyCN: reaction 意为「相互作用」，因此这个短语命名的是两种物质彼此作用时发生的事。

senses.title: Heat released or absorbed
senses.definition: the same process described by whether it warms its surroundings or draws heat in
senses.definitionCN: 同一过程按它使周围变热还是吸走热量来描述的两种情形
senses.example: The chemical reaction in the hand warmer releases heat for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 暖手宝里的化学反应会持续放热数小时。
senses.why: Breaking and forming bonds either costs or releases energy, so every reaction can be placed on a heat scale.
senses.whyCN: 化学键的断裂与形成要么消耗能量、要么释放能量，因此每个反应都能放在一条热量尺度上。

senses.title: Types of reaction
senses.titleCN: 反应类型：化合、分解、置换等
senses.definition: a classification such as combination, decomposition, displacement or double displacement
senses.definitionCN: 按化合、分解、置换或复分解等方式划分的类别
senses.example: The teacher drew a displacement chemical reaction on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在黑板上画了一个置换反应。
senses.why: Classification follows the pattern of what leaves and what joins, so the phrase is reused as a label for each pattern.
senses.whyCN: 分类依据的是哪些成分离开、哪些成分结合，因此这个短语被反复用作各类模式的标签。

senses.title: Rate and conditions
senses.definition: the speed of the process and the temperature, pressure or catalyst that control it
senses.definitionCN: 该过程进行的快慢，以及控制它的温度、压强或催化剂
senses.example: A catalyst speeds up the chemical reaction without being consumed.
senses.exampleCN: 催化剂能加快化学反应而不被消耗。
senses.why: Industry cares how fast a batch finishes, so the phrase often appears alongside rate, time and yield.
senses.whyCN: 工业关心一批料多快做完，因此这个短语常与速率、时间和产率一起出现。

senses.title: Reversible reactions and equilibrium
senses.definition: a process that can run backwards, settling at a balance between forward and reverse change
senses.definitionCN: 能反向进行、并在正逆变化之间达到平衡的过程
senses.example: In a closed tube the chemical reaction reaches equilibrium and appears to stop.
senses.exampleCN: 在封闭管中，该化学反应达到平衡，表面看像停止了。
senses.why: Because many reactions do not run to completion, the same phrase covers the two-way case and its balance point.
senses.whyCN: 许多反应并不会进行到底，因此同一短语也覆盖双向进行的情形及其平衡点。

senses.title: Reactions inside living things
senses.definition: the reactions of metabolism, such as digestion or respiration, that keep an organism alive
senses.definitionCN: 消化、呼吸这类维持生物体存活的代谢反应
senses.example: Enzymes control every chemical reaction that keeps the cell alive.
senses.exampleCN: 酶控制着维持细胞存活的每一个化学反应。
senses.why: Biochemistry applies the same phrase to cells, adding the idea that the reactions are guided by proteins.
senses.whyCN: 生物化学把这同一短语用于细胞，并附加了「反应由蛋白质引导」这一层意思。

senses.title: A chain of consequences
senses.definition: a figurative use for one event setting off a series of related changes
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指一个事件引发一连串相关变化
senses.example: The tariff set off a chemical reaction across three industries.
senses.exampleCN: 这项关税在三个行业间引发了一连串反应。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the idea that a small trigger can change the whole mixture, not just its starting point.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻借用了「少量触发物能改变整锅混合物」的观念，而不只是改变起始处。

senses.title: Instant personal chemistry
senses.titleCN: 口语：人与人之间立刻来电或立刻不合
senses.definition: an informal use for an immediate, almost physical attraction or clash between two people
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，指两人之间立刻产生近乎本能的吸引或冲突
senses.example: There was an obvious chemical reaction when the two leads first read together.
senses.exampleCN: 两位主角第一次对台词时，明显立刻有了化学反应。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrowed the laboratory phrase because attraction also feels like something happening beyond deliberate choice.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语借用实验室的说法，因为吸引力也像是发生在自觉选择之外的事情。

intro.en: The phrase joins chemical, from Greek khēmeia through Arabic al-kīmiyā, with reaction, from Latin re- back plus agere to do. Reaction first meant any response and was narrowed to chemical processes in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
intro.cn: 这个短语把 chemical 与 reaction 结合：前者来自希腊 khēmeia 并经阿拉伯语 al-kīmiyā，后者由拉丁 re-「回」加 agere「做」构成。reaction 最初指任何回应，十七、十八世纪才收窄到化学过程。

items.en: Agere meant to drive, do or act, and its participle actus underlies act, action and reaction.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、做、行动，其分词 actus 是 act、action 与 reaction 的共同基础。

items.en: Latin reagere meant to act back or act in return, so reaction began as the answer one thing gives to another.
items.cn: 拉丁 reagere 意为反过来作用、回应，因此 reaction 最初指一物对另一物给出的回应。

items.en: From the seventeenth century experimenters described two substances acting on each other as a reaction, and the phrase chemical reaction fixed that usage.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，实验者把两种物质彼此作用描述为 reaction，chemical reaction 这一短语把该用法固定下来。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry added rate, equilibrium and catalysis, so the phrase also came to name a quantity that can be timed and balanced.
items.cn: 十九世纪的化学加入了速率、平衡与催化，于是这个短语也开始指可以被计时和配平的量。

items.en: Modern journalism and everyday speech applied the phrase to social chains and personal attraction, keeping the image of one thing setting another off.
items.cn: 现代新闻与日常口语把这个短语用到社会连锁与个人吸引上，保留了「一物触发另一物」的意象。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built on the same chemical or reaction element; group two holds neighbouring process words that are often confused with a reaction.
note.cn: 第一组是含相同 chemical 或 reaction 成分的短语；第二组是容易被误当成反应的过程词。

entries.definition: The kind of change a reaction produces, named by its result; textbooks contrast it with physical change.
entries.definitionCN: 指反应所产生的那类变化，以结果命名；教科书把它与物理变化对照。

entries.definition: The symbolic record of a reaction, showing reactants and products with coefficients.
entries.definitionCN: 反应的符号记录，用系数列出反应物与生成物。

entries.definition: A process that alters atomic nuclei and releases far more energy; electrons are untouched.
entries.definitionCN: 改变原子核并释放远多能量的过程；电子并不参与。

entries.definition: Any response, from a person's reply to a chemical process; the full phrase narrows it to substances.
entries.definitionCN: 任何回应，从人的反应到化学过程；完整短语把它收窄到物质。

entries.definition: A change of shape, state or size with no new substance formed, such as melting ice.
entries.definitionCN: 形状、状态或大小的改变，不产生新物质，例如冰融化。

entries.definition: Any series of steps producing a result; a reaction is one kind of process with new substances as its result.
entries.definitionCN: 产生结果的任何一系列步骤；反应是其中以新物质为结果的一类。

entries.definition: A thorough change of form; it stresses the end state rather than the mechanism that brings it about.
entries.definitionCN: 形式上的彻底改变；侧重最终状态，而非造成改变的作用机制。

entries.definition: Any mutual effect between things; it becomes a reaction only when new substances form.
entries.definitionCN: 事物之间的任何相互影响；只有形成新物质时才成为反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, real textbook pairs and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实教科书对照与真实搭配。

normal.en: Re- plus act equals acting back: two substances act on each other.
normal.cn: re- 加 act 就是「反过来作用」：两种物质彼此作用。

normal.en: Reactant in, product out: the two words frame every reaction.
normal.cn: 反应物进去，生成物出来：这两个词框住了每一个反应。

normal.en: Chemical change is the result, chemical reaction is the event.
normal.cn: 化学变化是结果，化学反应是事件。

normal.en: Exothermic and endothermic mark the heat direction of a reaction.
normal.cn: 放热与吸热标出反应的热量方向。

normal.en: A catalyst changes the speed, never the reactants.
normal.cn: 催化剂改变速度，从不改变反应物。

abstract.en: Picture a match struck in a dark room: one small action sets the whole mixture alight.
abstract.cn: 想象在暗室里划亮一根火柴：一个微小动作点燃了整团混合物。

abstract.en: Picture a seesaw that settles and then looks perfectly still while both ends still move.
abstract.cn: 想象一架跷跷板停下来看似纹丝不动，其实两端仍在动。

abstract.en: Picture blue ink dropped into clear water until every part of the glass has changed colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴蓝墨落进清水，直到整杯水都换了颜色。

examples.en: A chemical reaction in the battery supplies the phone with current.
examples.cn: 电池里的化学反应为手机提供电流。

examples.en: The experiment failed because the chemical reaction ran too slowly.
examples.cn: 实验失败是因为化学反应进行得太慢。

examples.en: Rusting is a slow chemical reaction that no paint can fully stop.
examples.cn: 生锈是一种缓慢的化学反应，任何油漆都无法完全阻止。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开米扣 瑞爱克神」——开瓶量米扣盖，两种东西一碰就翻脸，正是化学反应

root: chemical（希腊 khēmeia 经阿拉伯语 al-kīmiyā、中世纪拉丁 alchimia，加拉丁 -alis）+ reaction（拉丁 re-「回、再」+ agere「做、驱动」的名词形式 reactio）；「物质彼此作用而生成新物质」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process viewed from different angles: the basic event, its heat, its type, its speed, its reversibility, its version inside a cell, and two figurative uses borrowed by journalism and everyday speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一过程的不同侧面：基本事件、热量、类型、速率、可逆性、细胞内的版本，以及被新闻与口语借走的两个比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two clear liquids meeting and turning green with bubbles.
core.cn: 核心意象：两瓶澄清液体相遇，变绿并冒起气泡。

branches.en: THE EVENT: atoms regroup and the starting materials are gone.
branches.cn: 事件：原子重新组合，原来的物质不再存在。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING AND NAMING: heat tells you the energy side, structure tells you the type.
branches.cn: 记账与命名：热量说明能量收支，结构说明反应类型。

branches.en: TIME: how fast it runs, and whether it can also run backwards.
branches.cn: 时间：它跑得多快，以及能否反向跑。

branches.en: CELLS: the same event, guided by enzymes, keeps an organism alive.
branches.cn: 细胞：同一事件在酶的引导下维持着生物体存活。

branches.en: METAPHOR: chains of consequences and instant attraction both borrow the laboratory image.
branches.cn: 比喻：连锁后果与即时吸引都借用了实验室的意象。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two analyzable words: chemical from the chem- stem, and reaction from re- plus the act- root plus -ion.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个可分析的词构成：chemical 来自 chem- 词干，reaction 由 re- 加 act- 词根再加 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Reaction is fully Latin in its pieces, while the chem- stem is Greek with an Arabic route. The Latin entries below therefore cover the re-, act- and -ion elements.
latinIntro.cn: reaction 的各个构件都来自拉丁语，而 chem- 词干来自希腊语并经过阿拉伯语。因此下面的拉丁词条覆盖 re-、act- 与 -ion 三部分。

items.example: Return, recall and react all begin with the same prefix.
items.exampleCN: return、recall 与 react 都以同一前缀开头。

items.structure: act- (Latin root from agere, to do or drive)
items.example: Action and agent grow from the same root.
items.exampleCN: action 与 agent 由同一词根长出。

items.example: Reaction names the act of acting back.
items.exampleCN: reaction 指「反过来作用」这一行为。

items.example: Sodium reacts violently with water.
items.exampleCN: 钠与水剧烈反应。

items.meaning: a response or a chemical process
items.example: The reaction produced a gas and a salt.
items.exampleCN: 该反应生成了一种气体和一种盐。

items.meaning: a substance that undergoes a reaction
items.example: Oxygen is a reactant in combustion.
items.exampleCN: 氧是燃烧中的一种反应物。

items.example: Reactive metals must be stored under oil.
items.exampleCN: 活泼金属必须存放在油下。

items.example: Reactivity falls down the group.
items.exampleCN: 反应活性沿该族向下递减。

items.meaning: a vessel where a reaction is carried out
items.meaningCN: 进行反应的容器或装置
items.example: The reactor was cooled before the next batch.
items.exampleCN: 下一批之前反应器被冷却了。

items.example: The stem appears in chemical and chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 该词干出现在 chemical 与 chemistry 中。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb agere (ag-, actum; to do or drive)
latinEntries.example: Latin agit means he does or drives.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 agit 意为「他做、他驱动」。

latinEntries.example: English react is built from the same re- plus act, not borrowed whole from Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 英语 react 用的是同一组 re- 加 act，并非整体借自拉丁语。

definition_zh: 游牧民；游牧部落成员；无固定居所的人；四处漂泊者
definition_en: a person who moves with herds or lives without a fixed home
core_image: 一个把全部家当系在驮架上的人，走到哪里就把门帘挂到哪里
scene: 井边支起一顶黑毡帐篷， A nomad waters the flock before the long crossing of the plain.
sceneCN: 这里 nomad 指「随畜群迁徙的游牧民」（第 1 个义项：以畜牧为生的游牧者）；句意为一位游牧民在穿越平原之前先给羊群饮水。图中可辨识物件：黑毡帐篷、水槽、羊群、驮架。

pos.zh: 游牧民；游牧部落成员；漂泊者

senses.title: A herder who moves with livestock
senses.definition: a person who moves seasonally with a herd to find pasture
senses.definitionCN: 按季节随畜群迁移以寻找草场的人
senses.example: The nomad knows which well still holds water in August.
senses.exampleCN: 这位游牧民知道哪口井到八月还有水。
senses.why: the Greek noun behind the word means one who roams for pasture, so herding is the oldest and tightest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的希腊名词意为「为放牧而游走者」，所以畜牧是最古老、最紧的义项。

senses.title: A person with no fixed home
senses.definition: a person who lives in no permanent dwelling
senses.definitionCN: 没有永久住所的人
senses.example: The city counted forty nomads sleeping under the arcade.
senses.exampleCN: 市里统计到有四十名无固定居所的人睡在拱廊下。
senses.why: the absence of a fixed address is enough to earn the name, even without animals.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有牲畜，只要没有固定地址，就足以得到这个称呼。

senses.title: A member of a nomadic people
senses.definition: a member of a society whose whole economy is organised around movement
senses.definitionCN: 整个经济都围绕移动来组织的社会中的成员
senses.example: The nomads of the steppe traded hides for iron at the frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 草原上的游牧民在边市用皮革换铁。
senses.why: the personal noun becomes a group label, because mobility is organised by the whole people rather than chosen by an individual.
senses.whyCN: 指人的名词变成群体标签，因为流动是由整个民族来组织的，而非个人选择。

senses.title: A restless traveller
senses.definition: a person who keeps moving out of temperament rather than necessity
senses.definitionCN: 因性情而非生计而不断移动的人
senses.example: He is a nomad by habit, never staying two winters in one town.
senses.exampleCN: 他习惯漂泊，从不在同一座镇上过两个冬天。
senses.why: the word loses its herds and keeps its restlessness, so it can describe a temperament.
senses.whyCN: 这个词丢掉了畜群，保留了不安定，因此可以形容性情。

senses.title: A remote worker who keeps moving
senses.titleCN: 不断更换驻地的远程工作者
senses.definition: a person who works online while changing cities or countries
senses.definitionCN: 一边在线工作一边更换城市或国家的人
senses.example: The island fills with nomads who stay for a month and leave.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛挤满了住一个月就走的数字游民。
senses.why: the old figure of the person whose livelihood travels is refilled with a laptop and a visa instead of a herd.
senses.whyCN: 「生计随身走」的旧形象被重新填上笔记本与签证，而不是畜群。

senses.title: An animal that roams
senses.definition: an animal that moves continuously rather than keeping a territory
senses.definitionCN: 持续移动、不守领地的动物
senses.example: The desert nomad among birds follows the rain front south.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类中的沙漠漫游者随雨锋南下。
senses.why: the human noun is transferred to animals mainly in natural-history writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个指人的名词主要在博物学写作中被移用到动物身上。

senses.title: A steppe or desert wanderer in history
senses.titleCN: 历史叙述中的草原或沙漠游牧者
senses.definition: a member of the mobile peoples of steppe or desert as described by settled neighbours
senses.definitionCN: 定居邻人笔下那些草原或沙漠中流动民族的成员
senses.example: The chronicle describes the nomad as a rider who carries his house on his back.
senses.exampleCN: 这部编年史把游牧民写成把房子背在背上的骑手。
senses.why: settled societies named mobile peoples from the outside, so the word carries an observer's viewpoint as well as a fact.
senses.whyCN: 定居社会是从外部给流动民族命名的，因此这个词既带事实，也带观察者的视角。

senses.title: Attributive use before a noun
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean nomadic, as in nomad camp
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前表示「游牧的」，如游牧营地
senses.example: A nomad tent can be struck in under an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 一顶游牧帐篷不到一小时就能拆完。
senses.why: English often lets a noun modify another noun, so nomad does the work of the adjective in tight compounds.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让名词修饰名词，因此在紧凑的复合词里，nomad 承担了形容词的职能。

intro.en: Nomad comes from Greek nomas, genitive nomados, 'roaming for pasture', through Latin and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nomad 出自希腊 nomas（属格 nomados）「为放牧而游走」，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nemein meant 'to pasture' and 'to deal out'. It belongs to a reconstructed root meaning 'to take, allot', a standard reconstruction with no direct attestation.
items.cn: nemein 意为「放牧」与「分配」。它属于意为「取、分配」的重构词根，这是学界常规重构，无直接书证。

items.en: Nomas named the person or animal that moves in search of grazing; the pasture, not the journey, was the point.
items.cn: nomas 指为找草而移动的人或畜；重点是草场，不是旅程。

items.en: Nomos 'law, custom' is a separate noun from the same verb; it produced economy and autonomy, and dictionaries that merge it with nomas are wrong.
items.cn: nomos「法、习俗」是同动词的另一个名词；它衍生 economy 与 autonomy，把它与 nomas 合并的词典是错的。

items.en: Latin kept nomas as a literary borrowing for a wandering shepherd, without developing a large family of its own.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 nomas 作为文学借词保留下来，指漂泊牧人，并未发展出庞大的本族词族。

items.en: French nomade widened the sense to any mobile people, and eighteenth-century travel writing spread the widened word.
items.cn: 法语 nomade 把词义放宽到任何流动民族，18 世纪游记把这一放宽后的词传播开来。

items.en: English nomad is recorded from the sixteenth century; the modern digital sense dates only from the twenty-first.
items.cn: 英语 nomad 自 16 世纪有记录；现代数字义直到 21 世纪才出现。

note.en: The first group is the same family or a Greek near neighbour; the second group names other kinds of mover, each with a different reason for moving.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词或希腊语近邻；第二组指其他类型的移动者，各自的移动理由不同。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the life; nomad is the person, nomadic is the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 描述这种生活的形容词；nomad 指人，nomadic 指性质。

entries.definition: The social and economic system of moving with herds; it cannot name one person.
entries.definitionCN: 随畜群移动的社会经济制度；不能指单个人。

entries.definition: The French form that English borrowed; the final -e is silent and should not be carried into English.
entries.definitionCN: 英语借用的法语形式；词尾 -e 不发音，不应带进英语拼写。

entries.definition: Greek for law or custom, from the same verb but not the same noun; it is behind economy, not nomad.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「法、习俗」，同动词但非同名词；它支撑 economy，而非 nomad。

entries.definition: Anyone who moves about without a fixed route; it lacks the herding and pasture history of nomad.
entries.definitionCN: 任何无固定路线四处走动的人；缺少 nomad 的畜牧与草场历史。

entries.definition: A person or animal that moves, usually between known places and for a known reason such as work or weather.
entries.definitionCN: 通常在已知地点之间、因工作或气候等已知原因而移动的人或动物。

entries.definition: An Arabic-speaking desert people of the Middle East; a proper name for one nomadic group, not a general term.
entries.definitionCN: 中东讲阿拉伯语的沙漠民族；是某一游牧群体的专名，不是通称。

entries.definition: A person who roams, often with a suggestion of pleasure or aimlessness rather than livelihood.
entries.definitionCN: 四处漫游的人，常暗示消遣或漫无目的，而非生计。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek pasture word, the family and the modern compounds the noun now forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语「草场」词、同族词，以及这个名词现在构成的现代复合词。

normal.en: nomas 'pasture-roamer' = the person; the tents and herds are implied by the Greek source.
normal.cn: nomas「为草场而游走者」= 这个人；希腊词源已隐含帐篷与畜群。

normal.en: The family runs nomad, nomadic, nomadism, seminomad and nomadically.
normal.cn: 词族包括 nomad、nomadic、nomadism、seminomad、nomadically。

normal.en: Common compounds are nomad camp, nomad tribe and digital nomad.
normal.cn: 常见复合词是「游牧营地」「游牧部落」「数字游民」。

normal.en: Greek nomos 'law' is behind economy and autonomy, not behind nomad.
normal.cn: 希腊 nomos「法」支撑 economy 与 autonomy，不支撑 nomad。

normal.en: The word is nearly always countable: a nomad, two nomads, the nomads of the steppe.
normal.cn: 这个词几乎总是可数：一个游牧民、两个游牧民、草原上的游牧民。

abstract.en: Picture a door curtain that can be hung on any frame in any valley.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅门帘，挂到任何山谷的任何门框上都合适。

abstract.en: Picture a saddlebag holding a bowl, a rope and a deed to nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鞍袋，装着一只碗、一根绳，和一张不指向任何地产的契。

abstract.en: Picture footprints that never deepen because they are never repeated.
abstract.cn: 想象一串永不加深的脚印，因为它们从不重复。

examples.en: The nomad traded two ewes for a sack of salt.
examples.cn: 这位游牧民拿两只母羊换了一袋盐。

examples.en: Nomads have crossed this pass for as long as the road has existed.
examples.cn: 自这条路存在以来，游牧民就一直翻越这道山口。

examples.en: She calls herself a digital nomad and works from six time zones.
examples.cn: 她自称数字游民，在六个时区之间工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺曼」听成「挪门」——门一挪就走，家当全在身上。挪门的人，就是游牧民。

root: 希腊 nomas（属格 nomados）「为放牧而游走」，出自 nemein「放牧、分配」；经拉丁 nomas 与法语 nomade 进入英语。同动词的 nomos「法、习俗」是另一条名词线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the herder to the homeless person, the whole people, the restless traveller, the remote worker, the roaming animal, the historical figure and finally the attributive use.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从牧人移到无家者、整个民族、不安定的旅人、远程工作者、漫游动物、历史形象，最后是定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller whose whole household is tied to a pack frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个把全部家当捆在驮架上的人。

branches.en: THE HERDER INSIDE AND OUTSIDE HISTORY: the working herder and the figure described by settled neighbours are the same person seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 历史内外的牧人：干活的牧人与定居邻人笔下的形象，是同一个人从两面看。

branches.en: WITHOUT A HOME, WITH OR WITHOUT A REASON: necessity and temperament both produce the same absence of address.
branches.cn: 没有家，有理由或没理由：生计与性情都造成同样的「没有地址」。

branches.en: THE WHOLE PEOPLE: mobility organised by a society turns the personal noun into an ethnic label.
branches.cn: 整个民族：由社会来组织的流动，把指人的名词变成族群标签。

branches.en: THE LAPTOP REPLACES THE HERD: remote work reproduces the old pattern with a different livelihood.
branches.cn: 笔记本取代畜群：远程工作用另一种生计复制了旧模式。

branches.en: ANIMALS AND COMPOUNDS: the noun is lent to roaming species and also pressed into service as a modifier.
branches.cn: 动物与复合词：这个名词既借给漫游物种，也被压作修饰语使用。

intro.en: Nomad is a Greek noun of pasturing with no Latin root, so its family is built by English suffixes rather than by Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: nomad 是希腊语「放牧」名词，没有拉丁词根，因此它的词族由英语后缀构成，而非拉丁前缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no native Latin relative: Latin only borrowed nomas. The Latin-looking nominal endings added later are English or French work, not Latin descent.
latinIntro.cn: 没有本族的拉丁亲戚：拉丁语只是借入 nomas。后来加上的那些拉丁味名词词尾是英语或法语的手工，而非拉丁血统。

items.example: The stem already contains the herd and the pasture.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干已包含畜群与草场。

items.example: The ending forms nomadic from nomad.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把 nomad 变成 nomadic。

items.example: The ending forms nomadism from nomad.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把 nomad 变成 nomadism。

items.example: A nomad keeps few possessions.
items.exampleCN: 游牧民的家当很少。

items.example: The nomads moved north with the rain.
items.exampleCN: 游牧民随雨向北移动。

items.example: The camp is nomadic in summer only.
items.exampleCN: 这个营地只在夏天流动。

items.example: Nomadism shapes the whole calendar.
items.exampleCN: 游牧制度塑造了整个历法。

items.example: The seminomad keeps a winter house.
items.exampleCN: 半游牧民有固定的冬屋。

items.example: They travelled nomadically for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 他们以游牧方式走了十年。

derivatives.meaning: the condition of being a nomad

definition_zh: 引证；举出（证据、理由）
definition_en: to offer facts or reasons as evidence in support of an argument
core_image: 把一摞证据一页页摆到辩论桌上
scene: 听证会上，律师翻开文件夹，把三份原始记录摆上桌。 The counsel adduced fresh documents to prove the timeline.
sceneCN: 这里 adduce 是「引证、举出」（第 1 个义项：提出证据或理由支持论点）；句意为律师出示新文件证明时间线。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「引证；举出证据」（另在解剖学中指内收）
同根词，义为「推断」，反方向使用同一词根

senses.title: To offer evidence for an argument
senses.definition: to put forward facts, documents, or examples as proof
senses.definitionCN: 提出事实、文件或例证作为证明
senses.example: The counsel adduced fresh documents to prove the timeline.
senses.exampleCN: 律师出示新文件证明时间线。
senses.why: Latin ducere means 'to lead'; to adduce is to lead evidence forward, out of the file and onto the table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ducere 意为「引导」；adduce 就是把证据从卷宗里领出来，引到桌面上。

senses.title: To cite reasons or examples
senses.definition: to mention reasons or instances in support of a claim
senses.definitionCN: 提及理由或实例以支持某个主张
senses.example: He adduced several precedents from earlier disputes.
senses.exampleCN: 他援引了早先争端中的几个先例。
senses.why: Reasons, like documents, are led out into the open where the audience can inspect them.
senses.whyCN: 理由如同文件，也要被领到明处，供听者查验。

intro.en: Adduce joins Latin ad- 'to' with ducere 'to lead', meaning 'to lead forward (as evidence)'.
intro.cn: adduce 由拉丁语 ad-（向）加 ducere（引导）构成，意为「把（证据）引上前」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *deuk- meant 'to lead, to pull'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *deuk- 意为「引导、牵拉」。

items.en: ducere meant 'to lead', the root of duke and duct.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导」，是 duke 与 duct 的词根。

items.en: adducere meant 'to lead to, to bring forward'.
items.cn: adducere 意为「引到、带来」。

items.en: English adduce settled into legal and scholarly argument.
items.cn: 英语 adduce 定着于法律与学术论证。

items.en: Now formal; everyday speech prefers cite or present.
items.cn: 如今属正式用语；日常口语多用 cite 或 present。

note.en: The first group gathers the ducere family; the second gathers verbs of putting forward proof.
note.cn: 第一组收 ducere 词族；第二组收提出证明的动词。

entries.definition: To work a conclusion out, leading thought downward from facts.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推断」，同一词根的反向使用。

entries.definition: To lead someone or something into a state.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「诱导、引起」。

entries.definition: An appendix; only the opening letters overlap, root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附录」；仅开头拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To mention a source or example as support.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引用、引证」。

entries.definition: To lay something before a court or audience.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提交、出示」。

entries.definition: To back a claim with solid evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证实、为主张提供依据」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the ducere root and the courtroom scene; the abstract hooks picture documents led onto a table.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 ducere 词根与法庭场景；抽象记忆点想象文件被引上桌。

normal.en: Adduce is ad- plus ducere: to lead evidence forward.
normal.cn: adduce 是 ad- 加 ducere：把证据引上前。

normal.en: Adduce evidence is the core collocation.
normal.cn: adduce evidence 是核心搭配。

normal.en: Deduce runs the same root in reverse: lead down to a conclusion.
normal.cn: deduce 把同一词根反过来用：引出结论。

normal.en: The word is formal, at home in law and scholarship.
normal.cn: 这个词很正式，常用于法律与学术。

normal.en: Everyday speech says cite instead.
normal.cn: 日常口语改用 cite。

abstract.en: Picture a lawyer sliding a folder across the bench.
abstract.cn: 想象律师把文件夹推过法官席。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of evidence pulled forward link by link.
abstract.cn: 想象证据链被一环环牵引向前。

abstract.en: Picture a teacher leading examples up onto the blackboard.
abstract.cn: 想象老师把例证引上黑板。

examples.en: The counsel adduced fresh documents to prove the timeline.
examples.cn: 律师出示新文件证明时间线。

examples.en: She adduced market data to support her forecast.
examples.cn: 她引用市场数据支持自己的预测。

examples.en: He adduced several precedents from earlier disputes.
examples.cn: 他援引了早先争端中的几个先例。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额丢斯」——把证据往桌上一丢就齐了，就是引证。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ ducere（引导）→ adducere（引上前）；核心义是「把证据或理由领到论辩的桌面上」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from offering documents as proof, to citing reasons and precedents.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从出示文件作证，走到援引理由与先例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evidence led forward onto the table
core.cn: 核心意象：证据被引上桌面

branches.en: Documents and facts led out as proof.
branches.cn: 被领出作证的事实与文件。

branches.en: Reasons and precedents led out in argument.
branches.cn: 论证中被援引的理由与先例。

branches.en: Both senses lead something out for inspection.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把某物领出来供查验。

branches.en: Legal argument is the natural home of this sense.
branches.cn: 法律论证是这个义项的自然阵地。

branches.en: Both stand on ducere, the Latin verb of leading.
branches.cn: 两者都立足拉丁语「引导」动词 ducere。

intro.en: The verb joins the prefix ad- with the lead-root duc-, and the ducere family spreads across deduce, induce, and conduct.
intro.cn: 这个动词把前缀 ad- 与「引导」词根 duc- 结合，ducere 词族遍布 deduce、induce 与 conduct。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere and its compound adducere are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 ducere 及其复合词 adducere。

definition_zh: 社会规范；一个群体共同接受、用来判断行为是否得体的规则
definition_en: a shared rule or expectation within a group about how its members ought to behave
core_image: 村口水井旁没有人维持秩序，后来的人却自动站到队尾，一条看不见的线把众人的动作排成同一顺序
scene: 北方小镇的集市上，摊位前没有人维持秩序，后来的人却自动站到队尾。 A social norm keeps the queue orderly even when no guard is present.
sceneCN: 这里 social norm 指群体共同接受、无须明说却约束行为的行为规则（第 1 个义项：共享的行为期待）；句意为一条社会规范让队伍在没有管理员时也保持整齐。

pos.zh: 社会规范；社会准则（可数，指一条具体规范时多用复数）
（社会学）某一群体共享的行为期待与评价标准

derivatives.zh: 规范；准则（由拉丁 norma「曲尺、规则」直接借入，指衡量行为的尺子）
规范的；应然的（由 norm 加表示「倾向」的拉丁后缀构成，转指「应当如何」的评价标准）
正常的；通常的（由 norma 加表示「属于」的拉丁后缀构成，从「合乎尺规」转指「合乎常规」）
使正常化；使标准化（由 normal 加表示「使成为」的后缀构成，转指使某物回到常规状态）
好交际的；合群的（由拉丁 socius「同伴」加表示「能……」的后缀构成，转指易于与人相伴）

senses.title: A shared rule of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 群体共同接受的行为规则
senses.definition: a rule about how people should behave that a group accepts and passes on
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体接受并沿袭的、关于人应当如何行为的规则
senses.example: A social norm keeps the queue orderly even when no guard is present.
senses.exampleCN: 一条社会规范让队伍在没有管理员时也保持整齐。
senses.why: The phrase joins a Latin word for a measuring square to a Latin word for a companion: a norm is the square against which a group measures behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把拉丁语里表示「曲尺」的词接到表示「同伴」的词上：规范就是群体用来量行为的尺子。

senses.title: An expectation backed by disapproval
senses.titleCN: 靠舆论与排斥维持的期待
senses.definition: an expectation whose breach brings frowns, gossip, exclusion or loss of trust rather than legal punishment
senses.definitionCN: 违反后会招来皱眉、闲话、排挤或失去信任，而非法律惩罚的期待
senses.example: Neighbours enforce the social norm by refusing to lend tools to anyone who never returns them.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们用「不借工具给有借无还的人」来执行这条社会规范。
senses.why: The group is the court: enforcement works through approval and withdrawal of approval, not through police.
senses.whyCN: 群体本身就是法庭：执行靠的是赞许与撤回赞许，而不是警察。

senses.title: Descriptive norm: what people actually do
senses.titleCN: 描述性规范：多数人实际怎么做
senses.definition: the behaviour that most members of a group actually perform, which others copy because it looks normal
senses.definitionCN: 群体中多数人实际做出的行为，旁人因为看上去正常而跟着照做
senses.example: Surveys show the descriptive norm is to recycle, even where no rule requires it.
senses.exampleCN: 调查显示，描述性规范是回收，即使没有规则要求。
senses.why: Sociologists split norms into two readings: the average behaviour and the approved behaviour. This sense is the average.
senses.whyCN: 社会学家把规范分成两种读法：多数人的实际行为与多数人赞成的行为。这个义项指前者。

senses.title: Injunctive norm: what people approve of
senses.titleCN: 指令性规范：多数人赞成什么
senses.definition: the behaviour that most members of a group approve or disapprove of, regardless of what they do themselves
senses.definitionCN: 群体中多数人赞成或不赞成的行为，与他们自己是否照做无关
senses.example: The injunctive norm says littering is wrong, yet many who say so still drop wrappers.
senses.exampleCN: 指令性规范认为乱扔垃圾不对，可许多这样说的人自己仍会丢包装纸。
senses.why: Approval is a separate track from practice: what people praise and what people do can pull in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 赞许与实行是两条轨道：人们称赞什么，与人们实际做什么，可能朝相反方向拉。

senses.title: An internalized obligation
senses.titleCN: 内化为个人义务的规范
senses.definition: a norm a person has absorbed so deeply that breaking it feels like personal guilt rather than public risk
senses.definitionCN: 一个人吸收得极深的规范，违反时感觉像个人愧疚，而不是怕被人看见
senses.example: She felt a pang of guilt for interrupting, so strong was the internalized norm.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为打断别人而感到一阵愧疚，这条内化的规范强到这种程度。
senses.why: Once the group's gaze moves inside the person, enforcement no longer needs witnesses.
senses.whyCN: 当群体的目光移进人的内心，执行就不再需要见证者。

senses.title: A formalized institutional standard
senses.titleCN: 制度化、成文化的行为标准
senses.definition: a norm written into the rules of a school, profession or organization and enforced by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 写进学校、行业或组织规则、由权威执行的规范
senses.example: The hospital turned courtesy into a formal social norm with a written code.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院把礼貌变成一条配有成文守则的正式社会规范。
senses.why: Institutions stabilize norms by writing them down, adding a sanction and a person whose job is to apply it.
senses.whyCN: 机构把规范写下来，再补上处罚与专门执行的人，规范因此稳定下来。

senses.title: A statistical regularity
senses.definition: the most common pattern in a set of observations, used as a baseline for judging what is unusual
senses.definitionCN: 一组观察中最常见的模式，用来判断什么算异常
senses.example: The study treated the social norm as the average number of children per household.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把每户平均子女数当作社会常规。
senses.why: Statistics borrows the word because an average is also a rule: it tells you what to expect before you look.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借用这个词，因为平均值也是一条规则：它在你观察之前就告诉你该期待什么。

senses.title: Abstract: any standard of correctness
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何正确性标准
senses.definition: any standard, explicit or implicit, by which a group decides that something is right or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 群体用来判定某事正确或可接受的任何标准，无论明说还是默认
senses.example: Every discipline develops its own social norm of what counts as a good question.
senses.exampleCN: 每门学科都会形成自己的社会规范，界定什么样的问题算好问题。
senses.why: At its widest the phrase means the measuring stick itself, apart from who holds it or what it measures.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个短语指的就是那把尺子本身，与谁拿着它、量什么都无关。

intro.en: The phrase couples Latin norma, a carpenter's measuring square, with socialis, 'of companions'. Its sociological sense is about a century old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语 norma（木匠的曲尺）与 socialis（同伴的）接在一起；它的社会学义大约只有一百年历史。年代均为约数。

items.en: Norma meant 'carpenter's square, rule, pattern'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a connection with Greek gnomon 'pointer on a sundial' has been suggested but is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: norma 意为「木匠的曲尺、规则、范型」。它更深的来源不确定；有人提出它与希腊语 gnomon「日晷指针」有关，但那只是假说。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally'. It is generally traced to Latin sequi 'to follow', from a reconstructed Indo-European root meaning 'to follow'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」。一般认为它可追溯到拉丁语 sequi「跟随」，其印欧词根为重构形式，意为「跟随」。

items.en: Socialis 'of companionship, of allies' gave French social and English social; the adjective names what is shared among companions.
items.cn: socialis「同伴的、盟友的」衍生法语 social 与英语 social；这个形容词指同伴之间共享的东西。

items.en: Social entered English in the sixteenth century. Norm followed much later as a learned borrowing from Latin, first as a rule or pattern in general.
items.cn: social 在十六世纪进入英语。norm 晚得多才作为学术借词从拉丁语进入，最初泛指规则或范型。

items.en: In early twentieth-century sociology norm narrowed to a standard of behaviour shared by a group, and social norm became a fixed phrase.
items.cn: 在二十世纪初的社会学中，norm 收窄为群体共享的行为标准，social norm 也随之成为固定说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded, the link between norma and gnomon is unproven, and the Indo-European root behind sequi is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：完整短语最早印行于何时没有记录；norma 与 gnomon 的联系未获证明；sequi 背后的印欧词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates the measuring square from words that only look or sound close; group two holds the neighbours that also guide behaviour.
note.cn: 第一组把这个「曲尺」与只是形近或音近的词分开；第二组是同样引导行为的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The rule itself, without the group. It can be a standard of behaviour or a statistical average; the full phrase adds the shared, group-wide dimension.
entries.definitionCN: 规则本身，不含群体这一层；它可以是行为标准，也可以是统计平均值，而完整短语补上了群体共享的维度。

entries.definition: Built on norma plus an adjective ending: conforming to a standard, hence ordinary. A normal act is not necessarily a norm.
entries.definitionCN: 由 norma 加形容词后缀构成：合乎标准，因而寻常；一个正常的行为不一定是规范。

entries.definition: From Latin enormis 'out of rule', literally the prefix for 'out' plus norma. It looks unrelated but shares the measuring-square root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 enormis「出了规矩」，字面是表示「向外」的前缀加 norma；看似无关，却同出「曲尺」词根。

entries.definition: From Latin forma 'shape, mould', not norma. It looks and sounds close but carries no rule sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 forma「形状、模子」，并非 norma；形音都近，却没有规则义。

entries.definition: An agreed practice, often explicit and formal; a norm can be unwritten and enforced only by disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 经约定形成的做法，往往明确而正式；规范可以不成文，只靠不赞许来执行。

entries.definition: A traditional way of doing something, handed down over time; it is usually older and more local than a norm.
entries.definitionCN: 世代沿袭的做法；通常比规范更古老、更具地方性。

entries.definition: The moral norms of a society, felt as strong and sacred; a norm can be merely procedural.
entries.definitionCN: 一个社会被视作强烈而神圣的道德规范；而规范可以只是程序性的。

entries.definition: An explicit instruction, as in a game or a school; a norm may never be written down.
entries.definitionCN: 明确的指令，如游戏或学校中的规定；规范则可能从不落成文字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Norma was a carpenter's square, so a norm is the square a group holds against your behaviour.
normal.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺，所以 norm 就是群体拿来量你行为的那把尺。

normal.en: Socius meant companion, so the full phrase is the rule companions share.
normal.cn: socius 意为同伴，所以这个完整说法就是同伴之间共享的规则。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the force: follow a norm, violate a norm, enforce a norm.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示约束力：遵守规范、违反规范、执行规范。

normal.en: Descriptive and injunctive are the two sociological readings: what people do and what people approve.
normal.cn: 描述性与指令性是两种社会学读法：人们实际怎么做，与人们赞成什么。

normal.en: The derived words keep the measuring idea: normative, normal, normalize.
normal.cn: 派生词保留「测量」的意象：规范的、正常的、使标准化。

abstract.en: Picture a queue forming without a sign, each newcomer reading the backs of the others.
abstract.cn: 想象队伍在没有标牌时自己形成，每个后来者都在读前面人的背影。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone lowers their voice at dusk without being told.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，黄昏时所有人不用谁提醒就压低声音。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler passed hand to hand, never seen, yet every hand measures by it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子被一只手递给另一只手，谁也看不见它，却都拿它来量。

examples.en: The village keeps the social norm that tools are returned the same evening.
examples.cn: 村里守着一条社会规范：工具当晚归还。

examples.en: Breaking a social norm can cost more trust than breaking a written rule.
examples.cn: 违反一条社会规范，失去的信任可能比违反一条成文规则更多。

examples.en: Sociologists distinguish the descriptive norm from the injunctive norm.
examples.cn: 社会学家把描述性规范与指令性规范区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜秀 诺姆」——社会同伴手里那把量行为的曲尺 → 社会规范

root: 拉丁 norma「木匠的曲尺、规则」+ 拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」；norma 更深来源不确定，socius 一般认为与 sequi「跟随」有关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the group's shared expectation to the two ways sociologists measure it, then inward to guilt, outward to written rules, and finally to the measuring stick itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从群体共享的期待出发，转到社会学家测量它的两种方式，再向内变成愧疚、向外变成成文规则，最后落到那把尺子本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group holds an invisible measuring square and quietly checks every member against it.
core.cn: 核心意象：群体握着一把看不见的曲尺，悄悄把每个成员对照它量一遍。

branches.en: THE GROUP AS COURT: a shared rule plus the approval and disapproval that enforce it.
branches.cn: 群体即法庭：共享的规则，加上执行它的赞许与不赞许。

branches.en: TWO READINGS: what members actually do versus what members approve of.
branches.cn: 两种读法：成员实际怎么做，对比成员赞成什么。

branches.en: INSIDE THE PERSON: the gaze is internalized, so guilt replaces witnesses.
branches.cn: 目光进入内心：规范被内化，愧疚取代了见证者。

branches.en: ON PAPER: institutions write the rule down and attach a sanction.
branches.cn: 落到纸上：机构把规则写下，并配上处罚。

branches.en: THE MEASURING STICK ITSELF: first a statistical average, then any standard of correctness.
branches.cn: 尺子本身：先指统计平均值，再指任何正确性标准。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two Latin stems, each of which also supports a small English family, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁词干构成，每个词干还支撑起一个小型英语词族，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma gives norm, normal and enormous; Latin socius gives social, society and sociable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 norma 衍生 norm、normal 与 enormous；拉丁 socius 衍生 social、society 与 sociable。

items.example: The root supplies the image of measurement.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「测量」的意象。

items.example: The root supplies the group.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「群体」这一层。

items.structure: socialis (of companions) through Old French to English
items.example: Social names what is shared among companions.
items.exampleCN: social 指同伴之间共享的东西。

items.example: Norm entered English as a learned word.
items.exampleCN: norm 作为学术词进入英语。

items.example: A normal reading is aligned with the square.
items.exampleCN: 正常的读法就是与曲尺对齐。

items.structure: norm plus a suffix meaning 'tending to'
items.example: Normative talk says what ought to be.
items.exampleCN: 规范性话语说的是「应当如何」。

items.example: Normalize turns a deviation back to the rule.
items.exampleCN: 使标准化就是把偏离拨回规则。

items.structure: socius plus a suffix of state or body
items.example: Society is the whole body of companions.
items.exampleCN: 社会就是同伴构成的整体。

items.meaningCN: 出了规矩的；因而巨大的
items.example: Enormous began as 'outside the square'.
items.exampleCN: enormous 最初意为「在曲尺之外」。

definition_zh: n. 表盘；刻度盘；拨号盘 v. 拨（号码）；打电话给
definition_en: a round marked face that shows a reading or is turned to select, or to make a telephone call by number
core_image: 收音机上的圆形刻度盘，指针停在两站之间；老式电话的转盘被手指拨到底再松开
scene: 他拨了急救电话。 He dialled the emergency number.
sceneCN: 第 3 个义项：dialled 指拨号；句意是他拨了急救电话。

senses.title: A marked face showing a reading
senses.definition: a round face with marks that shows a measurement or setting
senses.definitionCN: 带刻度、显示测量值或设置的圆面
senses.example: The dial on the radio stopped between stations.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机上的刻度盘停在两站之间。
senses.why: A pointer resting between two marks on a round scale.
senses.whyCN: 圆形刻度上停在两个标记之间的指针。

senses.title: A disc turned to select
senses.definition: a disc with finger holes turned to select a telephone number

senses.example: The old phone had a rotary dial.

senses.why: A finger pulling a numbered disc round to a stop.

senses.title: To call by number
senses.definition: to make a telephone call by pressing or turning the numbers
senses.definitionCN: 通过按键或转盘输入号码来打电话
senses.example: He dialled the emergency number.
senses.exampleCN: 他拨了急救电话。
senses.why: A thumb pressing the last digit on a keypad.

intro.en: Dial comes from Latin dies, day, through dialis, daily, because the first dial was a sundial that told the hour by the sun.
intro.cn: dial 源自拉丁语 dies（日、白天），经 dialis（每日的）而来，因为最早的 dial 是靠太阳报时的日晷。

items.en: Dies meant day.
items.cn: dies 意为白天、日。

items.en: Dialis meant daily.
items.cn: dialis 意为每日的。

items.en: Dialis came to name a sundial.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 dialis 转而指日晷。

items.en: Dial entered English for a sundial face.
items.cn: 十五世纪 dial 以日晷盘面义进入英语。

items.en: It moved to instrument faces and then phones.
items.cn: 十九世纪它转到仪表盘，再转到电话。

items.en: Dial now means making a call.
items.cn: 如今 dial 指打电话。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the di- day family and warns about dialysis; the near-meaning group names other ways of calling or reading a scale.
note.cn: 形近组共享 di-（日）家族，并提醒 dialysis 是另一个词；近义组是其他表示「打电话」或「读刻度」的词。

entries.definition: A daily record; it shares dies but records days in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 每日记录；共享 dies，但是用文字记录日子。

entries.definition: Active in the daytime; it shares dies through diurnus.
entries.definitionCN: 白天活动的；经 diurnus 共享 dies。

entries.definition: Filtering the blood; it looks similar but comes from Greek dialysis, a separating.
entries.definitionCN: 过滤血液；形似但来自希腊语 dialysis（分离）。

entries.definition: To telephone someone.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人打电话。

entries.definition: To telephone someone; the common British verb.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人打电话；英国常用动词。

entries.definition: An instrument that shows a measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 显示测量值的仪表。

normalIntro.en: Dial is di- day: the first dial was a sundial, so any marked round face took the name.
normalIntro.cn: dial 就是 di-（日）：最早的 dial 是日晷，于是任何带刻度的圆面都叫这个名字。

normal.en: Di- here means day, as in diary.
normal.cn: 这里的 di- 意为日，如 diary。

normal.en: A sundial was the first dial.
normal.cn: 日晷是最早的 dial。

normal.en: Dial a number means make a call.
normal.cn: dial a number 就是打电话。

normal.en: British doubles the l: dialled.
normal.cn: 英式双写 l：dialled。

normal.en: Dialysis is a different Greek root.
normal.cn: dialysis 是另一个希腊词根。

examples.en: He was dialling when the line dropped.
examples.cn: 他正在拨号时线路断了。

sensesIntro.cn: 同一个被转动的圆面：收音机刻度、带数字的圆盘与按键板。

core.cn: 核心意象：圆形收音机刻度上停在两个标记之间的指针

definition_zh: 本质；实质；精华；香精
definition_en: the basic nature of something, its most important quality, or a concentrated extract used for flavour or scent
core_image: 一层层剥掉外壳后，剩下的那一小滴最浓的东西
scene: 调香师把一大筐花瓣倒进蒸馏器，最后瓶底只留下一小滴香气最浓的液体。 The perfumer distilled a basket of petals and kept a few drops of essence.
sceneCN: 这里 essence 是「香精、精华」（第 3 个义项：从植物中提取的浓缩液）；句意：调香师蒸馏了一筐花瓣，只留下几滴香精。

derivatives.zh: essence 加形容词后缀 -ial，指「本质的；必不可少的」
essential 加副词后缀 -ly，指「本质上；基本上」
quint-（第五）加 essence 构成，指「精华；典范」，源出炼金术的第五元素

senses.title: The intrinsic nature of a thing
senses.definition: the set of qualities that make a thing what it is and not something else
senses.definitionCN: 使一事物成为该事物、而不是别的事物的那些根本性质
senses.example: Philosophers asked what the essence of a human being might be.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问人的本质究竟是什么。
senses.why: Cicero coined Latin essentia from the verb esse, to be, so the word names the being of a thing rather than its surface.
senses.whyCN: 西塞罗用动词 esse（是、存在）造出拉丁语 essentia，因此这个词命名的是事物的「存在本身」，而不是它的表面。

senses.title: The central point of something said or made
senses.definition: the most important idea or quality of something, especially when it can be put briefly
senses.definitionCN: 某事物最重要的想法或品质，尤指可以简短说出来的那部分
senses.example: The essence of her argument is that speed has a cost.
senses.exampleCN: 她论点的核心是：速度是有代价的。
senses.why: If essence is what a thing is, then the essence of a speech or a plan is the part without which it would no longer be itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然 essence 指一物之所是，那么一段讲话或一个计划的「essence」，就是缺了它便不再是它自己的那部分。

senses.title: A concentrated extract
senses.definition: a strong liquid drawn from a plant or food, used to give flavour or scent
senses.definitionCN: 从植物或食物中提取的浓液，用来提供味道或香气
senses.example: Add a few drops of vanilla essence to the cake mixture.
senses.exampleCN: 往蛋糕糊里加几滴香草香精。
senses.why: Alchemists spoke of a quinta essentia, a fifth and purest element, and from that idea the word came to name the purified concentrate of a substance.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术士讲「quinta essentia」，即第五种、最纯的元素；从这个观念出发，这个词开始指物质被提纯后的浓缩部分。

intro.en: Essence comes from Latin essentia, a philosophical coinage by Cicero rendering Greek ousia, built on the verb esse, to be.
intro.cn: essence 来自拉丁语 essentia，这是西塞罗为翻译希腊语 ousia 而造出的哲学术语，根基是动词 esse（是、存在）。

items.en: Esse means to be, and it is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: esse 意为「是、存在」，是这一整族词的根基。

items.en: Cicero coins essentia to render the Greek word ousia, the being of a thing.
items.cn: 西塞罗造出 essentia，用来翻译希腊语 ousia，即事物的「存在」。

items.en: The ending -entia forms abstract nouns of state, as in prudentia and patientia.
items.cn: 词尾 -entia 构成表示状态的名词，如 prudentia 与 patientia。

items.en: Essence carries the philosophical noun into French.
items.cn: essence 把这个哲学名词带入法语。

items.en: Essence appears in English in the fourteenth century, first in philosophical writing.
items.cn: essence 在十四世纪进入英语，最早出现在哲学写作中。

items.en: From the idea of a quinta essentia, the purest fifth element, the word later names concentrated flavourings and scents.
items.cn: 由「第五元素」quinta essentia 的观念出发，这个词后来指浓缩的调味液与香气。

note.en: Essence is the noun of being, close in form to essential and quintessence and in meaning to nature, substance, and extract.
note.cn: essence 是表示「存在」的名词，形式上与 essential、quintessence 相近，意义上与 nature、substance、extract 相邻。

entries.definition: absolutely necessary, or relating to the inner nature of something
entries.definitionCN: 必不可少的；与内在本质有关的

entries.definition: in basic nature, when everything else is stripped away
entries.definitionCN: 本质上；基本上

entries.definition: the purest and most perfect example of a quality
entries.definitionCN: 某品质最纯粹、最完美的体现（由拉丁语「第五元素」构成）

entries.definition: the usual character of a person or thing
entries.definitionCN: 人或事物通常具有的特性

entries.definition: the real matter or the most important content of something
entries.definitionCN: 某物的实体或其最重要的内容

entries.definition: a concentrated substance taken out of a plant or food
entries.definitionCN: 从植物或食物中提取出的浓缩物

normalIntro.en: Essence is the noun of being: it comes from esse, and the whole family of essential and quintessence grows from it.
normalIntro.cn: essence 是表示「存在」的名词，来自 esse，essential 与 quintessence 这一族词都从它长出来。

normal.en: The verb esse, to be, is the root of essence, essential, and essentially.
normal.cn: 动词 esse（是、存在）是 essence、essential 与 essentially 的根。

normal.en: Quintessence is quinta essentia, the fifth and purest element of the alchemists.
normal.cn: quintessence 即「quinta essentia」，是炼金术士所说的第五种、最纯的元素。

normal.en: In essence means in its basic nature, once details are set aside.
normal.cn: 「in essence」意为本质上，即把细节放到一边之后。

normal.en: If something is of the essence, it is absolutely necessary.
normal.cn: 如果某事「of the essence」，那就是绝对不可缺少的。

normal.en: Compare nature and substance: nature is how a thing behaves, substance is what it is made of.
normal.cn: 对比 nature 与 substance：nature 是事物的表现方式，substance 是它由什么构成。

abstract.en: Picture peeling an onion layer by layer until only a tiny core is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一层层剥开洋葱，最后只剩下一小颗核心。

abstract.en: Imagine a long speech being boiled down to one short sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一段很长的讲话被熬成一句很短的话。

abstract.en: Think of a hundred roses squeezed into one small bottle of oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一百朵玫瑰被压进一小瓶精油里。

examples.en: The essence of the treaty is a promise not to attack.
examples.cn: 这份条约的实质是承诺不发动攻击。

examples.en: She added a few drops of essence to the cream.
examples.cn: 她往奶油里加了几滴香精。

examples.en: In a rescue like this, time is of the essence.
examples.cn: 在这样的救援中，时间至关重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「es + sence」——后半截像「sense」（感觉），把一层层感觉剥掉，剩下的才是本质；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 esse（是、存在）→ 西塞罗仿希腊语 ousia 造出 essentia（本质）→ 古法语 essence → 英语 essence，核心义「使一物成为该物的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Essence begins as the philosophical being of a thing, narrows to the central point of a statement, and widens again to a purified concentrate.
sensesIntro.cn: essence 先是事物在哲学意义上的「存在」，再收窄为一段话的要点，最后又扩展为被提纯的浓缩物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the small pure drop that remains after everything else is boiled away.
core.cn: 核心意象：把别的东西都熬掉之后，剩下的那一小滴纯净物。

branches.en: The philosophical sense names what makes a thing what it is.
branches.cn: 哲学义命名的是使一物成为该物的东西。

branches.en: The central-point sense applies that inner core to words and plans.
branches.cn: 要点义把这个内在核心用到言辞和计划上。

branches.en: The extract sense makes the core something physical and concentrated.
branches.cn: 提取物义把这个核心变成可触摸的浓缩物。

branches.en: Both answer the question of what something really is once details are removed.
branches.cn: 两者都在回答：去掉细节之后，某物究竟是什么。

branches.en: Both point to a purified core, one abstract and one chemical.
branches.cn: 两者都指向被提纯的核心，一个抽象，一个物质。

intro.en: Essence belongs to the Latin verb esse, to be, and English builds essential, essentially, and quintessence on the same stem.
intro.cn: essence 属于拉丁语动词 esse（是、存在）一族，英语在同一词干上构成 essential、essentially 与 quintessence。

latinIntro.en: Latin esse means to be; essentia, coined by Cicero, means the being of a thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 esse 意为「是、存在」；西塞罗造出的 essentia 意为事物的存在。

items.example: Esse is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: esse 是这一族词的基础动词。

items.example: Essentia was the coinage of Cicero for Greek ousia.
items.exampleCN: essentia 是西塞罗为希腊语 ousia 造的译名。

items.example: The suffix -entia turns a stem into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -entia 把词干变成抽象名词。

items.example: Essence keeps the philosophical sense.
items.exampleCN: essence 保留了哲学含义。

items.example: Essential is the adjective of the same stem.
items.exampleCN: essential 是同词干的形容词。

items.example: Essentially adds the adverb ending.
items.exampleCN: essentially 加上副词结尾。

items.meaning: the fifth essence, the purest part
items.example: Quintessence joins quinta to essentia.
items.exampleCN: quintessence 把 quinta 与 essentia 组合起来。

items.example: Quinta essentia named the purest element above fire, air, water, and earth.
items.exampleCN: quinta essentia 指火、气、水、土之上最纯的元素。

items.meaning: the view that things have fixed essences
items.meaningCN: 认为事物具有固定本质的学说
items.example: Essentialism extends the noun into philosophy.
items.exampleCN: essentialism 把这个名词延伸到哲学。

definition_zh: 银行家；银行经理或高级职员；也指赌局中的庄家
definition_en: a senior officer or owner of a bank; also the person who keeps the table's funds in some gambling games
core_image: 一位穿西装的人坐在银行柜台后的办公室里，手边是账册与印章；牌桌另一端，另一个人守着筹码箱
scene: 分行经理在贷款文件上盖章，随后把副本交给客户。 The banker refused to lend more until the accounts were audited.
sceneCN: 此处指「银行经理或高级职员」（第 1 个义项：银行中的高级任职者）；句意为这位银行经理坚持账目审计完成前不再放贷。图中可辨识物件：账册、印章、贷款文件、筹码箱（用于对照赌博义）。

pos.zh: 银行家；银行经理或高级职员

senses.title: A senior bank officer
senses.definition: a senior manager or officer who works in a bank and decides on loans and accounts
senses.definitionCN: 在银行工作、负责贷款与账户的高级经理或职员
senses.example: The banker refused to lend more until the accounts were audited.
senses.exampleCN: 这位银行经理坚持账目审计完成前不再放贷。
senses.why: The agent suffix marks the person who does the bank's work, so the first sense is a senior person inside the institution.
senses.whyCN: 施动后缀标示做银行业务的人，因此第一义就是机构内的高级任职者。

senses.title: An owner or principal of a bank
senses.titleCN: 银行所有者或主要负责人
senses.definition: the owner or principal of a banking house, especially in private banking
senses.definitionCN: 银行钱庄的所有者或主要负责人，尤指私人银行
senses.example: The banker staked his own fortune on the new branch.
senses.exampleCN: 这位银行家把自己的财产押在新分行上。
senses.why: Where banks were family firms, the person who owned the house was the bank, and the word kept that personal sense.
senses.whyCN: 当银行是家族企业时，拥有钱庄的人就是银行，这个词保留了这种人身义。

senses.title: An investment banker
senses.definition: a professional who raises capital and advises on mergers, acquisitions and securities
senses.definitionCN: 负责筹资并就并购与证券提供建议的专业人士
senses.example: The investment banker valued the company before the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 投资银行家在出售前对这家公司作了估值。
senses.why: Investment banking created a separate professional identity, and the word followed that specialisation.
senses.whyCN: 投资银行业务造就了独立的职业身份，这个词也随之专指这一行。

senses.title: A central banker
senses.definition: an official of a central bank who sets monetary policy or supervises the banking system
senses.definitionCN: 制定货币政策或监督银行体系的中央银行官员
senses.example: Central bankers met to discuss the interest rate.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行家们开会讨论利率。
senses.why: Public monetary authority is a distinct role, and the word with central in front names its officials.
senses.whyCN: 公共货币当局是另一种角色，这个词加「中央」即指其官员。

senses.title: The keeper of a gambling table's funds
senses.definition: the person who holds and pays out the table's money in certain gambling games
senses.definitionCN: 在某些赌局中保管并支付桌面资金的人
senses.example: The banker dealt the cards and covered the bets.
senses.exampleCN: 庄家发牌并赔付赌注。
senses.why: A bank also meant a reserve of money, so the person who kept the table's reserve took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指一笔资金储备，掌管桌面储备的人因此得了同一个名称。

senses.title: The house side in a game
senses.definition: the side that holds the reserve and against which other players bet
senses.definitionCN: 持有资金储备、其他玩家与之对赌的一方
senses.example: The banker won back the losses in the last round.
senses.exampleCN: 庄家方在最后一局赢回了损失。
senses.why: The person and the side blur in play, so the word also names the house as an opponent.
senses.whyCN: 在牌局中人与一方会混同，因此这个词也指作为对手的庄家。

senses.title: An informal certainty
senses.definition: something regarded as certain to succeed, used in informal British speech
senses.definitionCN: 被认为必定成功的事，用于非正式的英式口语
senses.example: The deal is a banker if the board agrees.
senses.exampleCN: 只要董事会同意，这笔交易就十拿九稳。
senses.why: A reliable bank was a safe place for money, and the person-word became slang for a sure thing.
senses.whyCN: 可靠的银行是存钱的安全处，指人的词因此成为表示「稳赢」的俚语。

senses.title: A financial adviser or expert
senses.definition: an expert who advises governments or firms on money, credit and financial structure
senses.definitionCN: 就金钱、信贷与财务结构向政府或公司提供建议的专家
senses.example: The treasury hired a banker to restructure its debt.
senses.exampleCN: 国库聘请一位金融专家重组债务。
senses.why: Expertise in money is a service, so the person-word also covers the advisory role outside a bank.
senses.whyCN: 金钱方面的专长是一种服务，因此这个指人的词也涵盖银行之外的顾问角色。

intro.en: Banker is bank plus an agent suffix from Latin -arius through French. The money sense of bank comes from Italian banca 'bench'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是「银行」加施动后缀，该后缀经法语来自拉丁语的施动者词尾。银行的金钱义来自意大利语 banca「长凳」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Banca named the bench where money was changed and then the business carried on there.
items.cn: banca 先指兑换钱币的长凳，后指在那里做的生意。

items.en: Medieval Latin bancus recorded the bench and the money trade and supplied the English form.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 bancus 记录了长凳与金钱交易，并提供英语形式。

items.en: English bank named the money business and the institution, and from it the person-word was formed.
items.cn: 英语以这个词指金钱生意与机构，再由它构成指人的词。

items.en: A French agent suffix from Latin -arius marked the person who performs the action, giving banker.
items.cn: 一个经法语来自拉丁的施动后缀标示执行动作的人，构成这个词。

items.en: Because a bank also meant a reserve of money, the keeper of a gambling table's reserve was called a banker too.
items.cn: 由于这个词也指资金储备，保管赌桌储备的人也被赋予了同一名称。

items.en: Attestation uncertain (first citation): the earliest recorded use of the person-word is not precisely dated, and the gambling sense may be older than the banking one.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：指人词的最早用例没有确切年代，赌博义可能比银行义更早。

note.en: Group one separates the person from the institution and the business; group two holds people who handle money and the rival role at a table.
note.cn: 第一组把人物与机构、业务分开；第二组是处理金钱的人与牌桌上的对手角色。

entries.definition: Bank is the institution or the verb; banker is the person who works in or owns it.
entries.definitionCN: bank 是机构或动词；banker 是在其中工作或拥有它的人。

entries.definition: Banking is the business carried on, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: banking 是从事的业务，不是人。

entries.definition: Bankable describes what a bank will accept, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: bankable 描述银行愿意接受的东西，不指人。

entries.definition: A broker matches buyers and sellers for a fee, a different function from a banker's lending and advising.
entries.definitionCN: broker 收取费用撮合买卖双方，与银行家的放贷和咨询职能不同。

entries.definition: A financier operates across institutions and large deals, while a banker usually works inside one bank.
entries.definitionCN: financier 跨机构与大型交易运作，banker 通常在一家银行内工作。

entries.definition: A teller serves customers at the counter, far below the senior officer a banker usually is.
entries.definitionCN: teller 在柜台服务客户，地位远低于通常意义上的银行高级职员。

entries.definition: A cashier keeps the till and handles payments, a narrower front-line role.
entries.definitionCN: cashier 掌管收银台并处理付款，是更窄的一线角色。

entries.definition: A dealer trades securities or holds the table's position, overlapping with the gambling sense but not the banking one.
entries.definitionCN: dealer 交易证券或持有桌面头寸，与赌博义重叠，却不属银行义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real agent suffix, the real bank family and the real double life of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的施动后缀、真实的银行词族与这个词真实的两面生活。

normal.en: The suffix marks the person: bank plus agent ending equals the one who does the bank's work.
normal.cn: 后缀标示人物：银行加施动词尾，就是在银行做事的人。

normal.en: It covers owners, senior officers, investment specialists and central officials.
normal.cn: 它涵盖所有者、高级职员、投资专家与中央官员。

normal.en: Because a bank can be a reserve, the keeper of a gambling reserve also takes the name.
normal.cn: 由于这个词也可指储备，保管赌局储备的人也得到这个名称。

normal.en: In informal British speech a banker is a sure thing, from the safety of a reliable bank.
normal.cn: 在非正式英式口语中，这个词指稳赢的事，源自可靠银行的安全感。

normal.en: It is a person word, unlike the institution and the industry beside it.
normal.cn: 它是指人的词，与旁边的机构和行业不同。

abstract.en: Picture a person behind a heavy door, deciding which projects will be funded.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人坐在厚重的门后，决定哪些项目能获得资金。

abstract.en: Picture a second person at a card table guarding a box of chips.
abstract.cn: 想象另一个人在牌桌旁守着一箱筹码。

abstract.en: Picture a word that can sit in an office and at a gaming table on the same day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词，同一天既能坐在办公室，也能坐在赌桌旁。

examples.en: The banker asked for two years of accounts before agreeing to the loan.
examples.cn: 这位银行家在同意贷款前要求提供两年的账目。

examples.en: Central bankers raised rates to slow the price rise.
examples.cn: 中央银行家提高利率以减缓物价上涨。

examples.en: At the card table the banker held the chips and paid the winners.
examples.cn: 牌桌上庄家持有筹码并赔付赢家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「板」加「客」——在长板桌后替人管钱、放贷的客人，就是银行家

root: 由「银行」加施动后缀构成，该后缀经法语来自拉丁语的施动者词尾；银行的金钱义来自意大利语 banca「长凳」，经中世纪拉丁 bancus 进入英语。因这个词亦指资金储备，赌局中掌管储备的人也得此名。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person: a senior officer becomes an owner, an investment specialist, a central official, a gambling keeper, the house side, an informal certainty and finally an adviser.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个人展开：高级职员先成为所有者、投资专家、中央官员、赌局掌管者、庄家一方、口语中的稳赢之事，最后成为顾问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person behind a bank's heavy door and another at a card table, sharing one name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在银行厚门之后，另一个人在牌桌旁，共用一个名字。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION'S PEOPLE: senior staff and the owning principal.
branches.cn: 机构中的人：高级职员与拥有银行的主要负责人。

branches.en: THE SPECIALISTS: deal-making bankers and public monetary officials.
branches.cn: 专家：做交易的银行家与公共货币官员。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the keeper of the reserve and the house side in play.
branches.cn: 牌桌：储备的掌管者与对赌的庄家一方。

branches.en: THE SLANG: a reliable bank becomes a sure thing.
branches.cn: 俚语：可靠的银行变成「稳赢的事」。

branches.en: THE ADVISER: money expertise sold outside a bank.
branches.cn: 顾问：在银行之外出售的金钱专长。

intro.en: Banker is a person-word built on the money word bank, and it shares the whole bank family.
intro.cn: 这个指人的词建立在金钱词「银行」之上，并共享整个银行词族。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin bancus supplies the money form; the agent suffix comes from Latin -arius through French.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁 bancus 提供金钱义形式；施动后缀经法语来自拉丁语的施动者词尾。

items.meaning: one who works in a bank
items.example: The banker approved the draft.
items.exampleCN: 银行家批准了汇票。

items.structure: Italian banca (bench) through Medieval Latin bancus
items.example: The bank closed early.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行提前关门。

items.example: Banking expanded abroad.
items.exampleCN: 银行业务向海外扩张。

items.example: The plan is bankable.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划可获得银行支持。

items.example: A backer supplied the bankroll.
items.exampleCN: 一位支持者提供了资金。

items.example: The banknote was old.
items.exampleCN: 这张纸币很旧。

items.example: The embankment was repaired.
items.exampleCN: 堤岸修好了。

items.example: The plane banked right.
items.exampleCN: 飞机向右倾斜。
