definition_zh: 冰川作用；冰期；冰川覆盖；冰川地貌的形成
definition_en: the process or period of being covered by glaciers, and the landforms and record that ice leaves behind
core_image: 山谷里一条冰川退去后，裸岩上留下磨光的石面和成堆碎石
scene: 山谷里的冰川退去之后，裸岩上留下磨光的石面和成堆的碎石。 Repeated glaciation polished the valley floor and left ridges of loose stone.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（冰川作用）；句意为反复的冰川作用把谷底磨光，并留下成脊的碎石。

pos.zh: 名词：冰川作用；冰期；冰川覆盖；冰川地貌的形成

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁「冰」词加形容词词尾构成，义为「冰川的；冰期的」
由「冰川」词干加动词词尾构成，义为「使受冰川作用；冻结」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「受过冰川作用的」
由否定前缀加「冰川作用」构成，义为「冰川消退」
由表示「之间」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「间冰期的」
由拉丁「冰」词经法语进入英语，义为「冰川」
由「冰川」词干加学科词尾构成，义为「冰川学」

senses.title: The process of ice covering the land
senses.definition: the growth and spread of glaciers over a landscape
senses.definitionCN: 指冰川在陆地上生成、扩张并覆盖地面的过程
senses.example: Glaciation begins where snow lasts all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 在积雪整夏不化的地方，冰川作用开始了。
senses.why: The noun ending turns the action of ice into a process that can be observed and dated.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾把冰的作用变成一种可观察、可测年的过程。

senses.title: A glacial period
senses.definition: a episode in Earth history when ice sheets expanded far beyond their present limits
senses.definitionCN: 指地球历史上冰盖远远超出当今范围的一段时期
senses.example: The last glaciation ended about eleven thousand years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 末次冰期约在一万一千年前结束。
senses.why: A process repeated many times becomes countable, and each episode gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 同一过程反复发生便变得可数，每一次都可以命名。

senses.title: The extent of ice cover
senses.definition: the area or share of a region that was covered by ice
senses.definitionCN: 指某一地区被冰覆盖的面积或比例
senses.example: The glaciation of the plateau reached its lowest slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 高原的冰川覆盖一直延伸到最低的山坡。
senses.why: Mapping turns the process into a boundary on a map.
senses.whyCN: 制图把这个过程变成地图上的一条界线。

senses.title: Landforms made by ice
senses.definition: the set of features produced by moving ice, such as U-shaped valleys, moraines and polished rock
senses.definitionCN: 指移动的冰所造成的一组地貌，如槽形谷、冰碛与磨光岩面
senses.example: The valley's glaciation is read from its polished walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这条谷地的冰川作用可从磨光的谷壁读出来。
senses.why: The word can name the results as well as the cause, because the results are what survive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指原因也可指结果，因为留存下来的正是结果。

senses.title: The geological record of past ice
senses.definition: the evidence in rock, sediment and landform that ice once covered an area
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石、沉积物与地貌中留下的、说明某地曾被冰覆盖的证据
senses.example: Scratches on the bedrock record ancient glaciation.
senses.exampleCN: 基岩上的擦痕记录了古老的冰川作用。
senses.why: Once the ice is gone, only traces remain, and the word shifts to the traces.
senses.whyCN: 冰退去之后只剩痕迹，这个词便转向这些痕迹。

senses.title: Alpine glaciation
senses.definition: glaciation confined to mountain valleys, where ice flows down existing channels
senses.definitionCN: 指局限于山谷的冰川作用，冰沿原有河道下流
senses.example: Alpine glaciation carves sharp ridges and deep cirques.
senses.exampleCN: 高山冰川作用刻出尖锐山脊与深冰斗。
senses.why: Mountain ice is channelled, so the landforms it makes are narrow and steep.
senses.whyCN: 山地冰川受地形约束，因此造成的形态狭窄而陡峭。

senses.title: Continental glaciation
senses.definition: glaciation by broad ice sheets that bury the landscape rather than follow valleys
senses.definitionCN: 指由宽阔冰盖造成的冰川作用，冰盖掩埋地景而不沿谷地下行
senses.example: Continental glaciation flattened the whole plain.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆冰川作用把整片平原削平。
senses.why: An ice sheet ignores the valleys beneath it, producing a very different signature.
senses.whyCN: 冰盖不理睬下面的谷地，留下的印记因而完全不同。

senses.title: The cooling that accompanies ice growth
senses.definition: the climatic cooling and drying associated with expanding ice
senses.definitionCN: 指与冰体扩张相关的气候变冷与变干
senses.example: Early glaciation lowered temperatures across the continent.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的冰川作用使整个大陆的气温下降。
senses.why: Ice both responds to climate and changes it, so the word carries a climatic echo.
senses.whyCN: 冰既响应气候又改变气候，这个词因此带上一层气候的回声。

intro.en: Glaciation rests on Latin glacies, ice, through the adjective glacialis and the Alpine word glacier. The noun with its process ending was formed in the nineteenth century, when geologists recognised that ice had once shaped whole landscapes; the exact coinage date is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语 glacies「冰」之上，经形容词 glacialis 与阿尔卑斯山区表示「冰川」的词进入欧洲语言。带过程词尾的名词在十九世纪形成，当时地质学家认识到冰曾经塑造整片地景；确切造词年份不确定。

items.en: Glacies meant ice, the solid form of water.
items.cn: 这个词意为冰，即水的固态。

items.en: The adjective meant icy or frozen, and it survives in the English word glacial.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为冰的、冻结的，英语中表示「冰川的」形容词由它而来。

items.en: Alpine French used a word for the moving ice of a valley, and English borrowed it in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 阿尔卑斯山区的法语用某个词指谷地中流动的冰，英语在十八世纪借入。

items.en: The adjective entered geology for ice and for periods of ice growth.
items.cn: 这个形容词进入地质学，指冰的或冰期扩张的。

items.en: Geologists added the process ending to name the action of ice on a landscape; the first use is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 地质学家加过程词尾，用来指冰对地景的作用；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century work dated successive ice advances and retreats, making the word countable and cyclic.
items.cn: 二十世纪的研究为一次次冰进与冰退测年，使这个词变得可数并带有旋回意味。

note.en: The first group shares the ice root or a derived ending; the second group names the periods, the ice bodies and the debris.
note.cn: 第一组共享「冰」词根或派生词尾；第二组是时期、冰体与碎屑的说法。

entries.definition: A mass of ice that moves slowly down a valley or across a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿谷地下行或横过大陆的缓慢移动冰体。

entries.definition: Relating to ice or to a glacial period.
entries.definitionCN: 指与冰或冰期有关的。

entries.definition: To subject a landscape to the action of ice.
entries.definitionCN: 指使地景受到冰的作用。

entries.definition: The retreat and melting of ice at the end of a glacial period.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰期结束时冰的退缩与融化。

entries.definition: A warmer interval between two glacial periods.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个冰期之间较温暖的间隔。

entries.definition: A long period when ice sheets were extensive.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰盖范围广大的漫长时期。

entries.definition: A single cold episode within an ice age.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个冰期内的一次寒冷阶段。

entries.definition: A broad dome of ice covering a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖大陆的宽阔冰穹。

entries.definition: Debris carried and dumped by a glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰川搬运并堆积的碎屑。

entries.definition: Unsorted sediment left directly by ice.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰直接留下的未经分选的沉积物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the Latin word for ice and the marks ice leaves.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着拉丁语的「冰」词与冰留下的痕迹展开。

normal.en: Ice plus a process ending: the work ice does to a landscape.
normal.cn: 冰加过程词尾，就是冰对地景所做的工作。

normal.en: A U-shaped valley and polished walls are the signature of mountain ice.
normal.cn: 槽形谷与磨光的谷壁是山地冰川的标志。

normal.en: Scratches on bedrock outlive the ice that cut them.
normal.cn: 基岩上的擦痕比刻出它的冰活得更久。

normal.en: An ice sheet ignores valleys and flattens everything beneath it.
normal.cn: 冰盖不理睬谷地，把下面的一切削平。

normal.en: Repeated advances make the word countable: one glaciation, then another.
normal.cn: 反复的冰进让这个词可数：一次冰期，又一次冰期。

abstract.en: Ice is a sculptor that leaves its tools behind as rubble.
abstract.cn: 冰是一位雕刻家，把工具留成了碎石。

abstract.en: A process can be named twice: once as an event, once as the shape it left.
abstract.cn: 同一过程可以被命名两次：一次作为事件，一次作为留下的形状。

abstract.en: What melts away can still be read in what it scratched.
abstract.cn: 融化消失之物，仍能从它划过的痕迹里读出。

examples.en: Continental glaciation buried the plain under a sheet of ice.
examples.cn: 大陆冰川作用把平原埋在一片冰盖之下。

examples.en: The cirque is a classic landform of alpine glaciation.
examples.cn: 冰斗是高山冰川作用的典型地貌。

examples.en: Dates of past glaciation come from rocks and sediments.
examples.cn: 历次冰川作用的年代来自岩石与沉积物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「格拉西艾申」——格拉西（冰）把山谷磨光又退走，留下一个冰期：冰川作用、冰期

root: 拉丁语 glacies「冰」经形容词 glacialis 与阿尔卑斯法语表示「冰川」的词进入英语；带过程词尾的名词于十九世纪形成，确切年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split the process from its episodes, its extent, its landforms, its traces, its mountain and continental styles, and its cooling effect.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把过程与其次序分开：过程本身、一次次冰期、覆盖范围、地貌、痕迹、山地与大陆两种样式，以及它带来的降温。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a retreating glacier exposing polished rock and ridges of loose debris.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条退缩的冰川露出磨光的岩石与成脊的碎屑。

branches.en: THE PROCESS AND ITS EPISODES: ice growing and spreading, then a named cold period.
branches.cn: 过程与阶段：冰生成、扩张，随后是一次具名的寒冷期。

branches.en: THE MAP: the area that ice covered.
branches.cn: 地图上的范围：冰曾经覆盖的区域。

branches.en: THE CARVING: landforms, in mountain valleys and under broad sheets.
branches.cn: 雕刻结果：山谷与冰盖之下形成的地貌。

branches.en: THE TRACES: scratches, sediment and erratics left after the melt.
branches.cn: 痕迹：融化后留下的擦痕、沉积物与漂砾。

branches.en: THE CLIMATE ECHO: cooling that accompanies the ice.
branches.cn: 气候回声：随冰而来的降温。

intro.en: The word is Latin ice with a process ending, plus a French word for the moving ice itself.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的「冰」加过程词尾，另有法语词指流动的冰本身。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the noun for ice and the adjective for icy; French supplies the name of the moving mass.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供「冰」的名词与「冰的」形容词；法语提供流动冰体的名称。

items.example: It is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整族词的词根。

items.example: It gives English glacial.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语中的「冰川的」。

items.example: English borrowed it for valley ice.
items.exampleCN: 英语借它指谷地中的冰。

items.example: The verb ending marks the action.
items.exampleCN: 动词词尾标记这一作用。

items.example: It turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The adjective is used for both ice and periods.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既指冰也指时期。

items.example: It forms the word for ice retreat.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示冰退的词。

items.example: It forms the word for warm intervals between ice ages.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示冰期之间暖期的词。

items.example: It forms glaciology, the study of ice.

definition_zh: 酶的；酶催化的；由酶完成的
definition_en: relating to an enzyme, or carried out with the help of an enzyme rather than by a chemical reagent
core_image: 一只戴着手套的手把两块原料按到一起，手套上印着小小的标签，说明这双手属于某个催化者
scene: 这里指「酶的」。 The enzymatic breakdown of starch begins in the mouth and continues in the small intestine.
sceneCN: 这里 enzymatic 指「酶促的、由酶完成的」（第 2 个义项：说明该过程依靠酶而非化学试剂进行）；淀粉的分解从口腔开始，到小肠继续。图中可辨识物件：戴手套的手、两块原料、催化剂标签、分解产物。

pos.zh: 酶的；酶催化的；由酶完成的（多作定语，修饰反应、水解、测定等）

senses.title: Belonging to an enzyme
senses.definition: relating to an enzyme as an object or a category
senses.definitionCN: 与酶这一对象或类别相关
senses.example: The enzymatic machinery of the lysosome is encoded by dozens of genes.
senses.exampleCN: 溶酶体的酶系统由数十个基因编码。
senses.why: the suffix adds a relation to the noun, so the adjective first answers 'whose?' or 'of what kind?'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀给名词加上关系，因此这个形容词首先回答「谁的」或「哪一类」。

senses.title: Carried out by an enzyme
senses.titleCN: 酶促的：由酶而非试剂完成
senses.definition: describing a reaction that is run by an enzyme instead of by heat or a chemical reagent
senses.definitionCN: 描述由酶而非加热或化学试剂推动的反应
senses.example: The conversion is enzymatic, so it happens at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这一转化是酶促的，因此在室温下即可发生。
senses.why: the adjective moves from the owner to the method: a reaction labelled enzymatic owes its speed to the catalyst.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从「所有者」转向「方法」：被标为 enzymatic 的反应，其速度归功于催化剂。

senses.title: The reaction as a category
senses.titleCN: 酶促反应的：作为一类过程
senses.definition: naming a whole class of reactions studied in biochemistry, as opposed to non-enzymatic ones
senses.definitionCN: 命名生物化学中一整类反应，以区别于非酶促反应
senses.example: Enzymatic reactions outnumber spontaneous ones in a living cell.
senses.exampleCN: 在活细胞中，酶促反应远多于自发反应。
senses.why: because the class is defined by its cause, the adjective can name the category rather than one event.
senses.whyCN: 由于该类由成因定义，这个形容词可以命名整个类别，而不是单个事件。

senses.title: Activity you can measure
senses.definition: describing the measurable activity of an enzyme in a sample
senses.definitionCN: 描述样本中可测定的酶活性
senses.example: Enzymatic activity fell sharply after the sample was heated.
senses.exampleCN: 样本加热后酶活性急剧下降。
senses.why: once the catalyst is assayed, 'enzymatic' also qualifies the quantity being measured.
senses.whyCN: 当催化剂被测定时，enzymatic 也用来限定被测定的那个量。

senses.title: Breakdown by enzyme
senses.definition: describing the splitting of a molecule into smaller pieces by enzymes
senses.definitionCN: 描述由酶把分子切成更小片段
senses.example: Enzymatic hydrolysis turns the protein into short peptides.
senses.exampleCN: 酶解把蛋白质变成短肽。
senses.why: digestion is the oldest use of catalysts, so the adjective attaches naturally to the cutting of bonds, as in enzymatic hydrolysis.
senses.whyCN: 消化是催化剂最古老的用途，因此这个形容词自然附着在断键上，如酶解。

senses.title: Assembly by enzyme
senses.definition: describing the building of a product with enzymes instead of chemical synthesis
senses.definitionCN: 描述用酶而非化学合成来制造产物
senses.example: Enzymatic synthesis avoids the toxic solvent used in the chemical route.
senses.exampleCN: 酶法合成避免了化学路线所用的有毒溶剂。
senses.why: the same catalyst that cuts can also join, so the adjective also marks a gentler way of building.
senses.whyCN: 能切的催化剂也能接，因此这个形容词也标记一种更温和的制造方式。

senses.title: Degradation by enzyme
senses.titleCN: 酶促降解的：被酶分解掉
senses.definition: describing the natural or engineered destruction of a substance by enzymes
senses.definitionCN: 描述某物质被酶自然或工程化地分解
senses.example: Enzymatic degradation removed the pesticide from the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 酶促降解把农药从土壤中清除。
senses.why: when the product must disappear, the adjective names the process that removes it rather than the one that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 当产物需要消失时，这个形容词命名的是清除过程，而不是制造过程。

senses.title: The control that has none
senses.titleCN: 对照义：与非酶过程相对
senses.definition: used contrastively, as in non-enzymatic, to mark what happens without a catalyst
senses.definitionCN: 用于对比，如 non-enzymatic，标记没有催化剂时发生的事
senses.example: The same sugar browned faster by the enzymatic route than by the non-enzymatic one.
senses.exampleCN: 同样的糖经酶促途径比非酶途径褐变得更快。
senses.why: science needs a control, so the adjective also lives in its negated form, defining the process by what it lacks.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要对照，因此这个形容词也活在否定形式中，用「缺少什么」来定义过程。

intro.en: Enzymatic is the English adjective on enzyme, with the suffix -atic, ultimately from Latin -aticus, itself from Greek -atikos. The base was coined in 1877.
intro.cn: enzymatic 是以 enzyme 为词干、加后缀 -atic 的英语形容词，-atic 源自拉丁 -aticus，后者又来自希腊 -atikos；词干造于 1877 年。

items.en: enzyme joins en- 'in' to zymē 'leaven'; the adjective inherits that compound without change.
items.cn: enzyme 把 en-「在内」与 zymē「酵素」结合；形容词原样继承这个合成词。

items.en: Latin -aticus formed adjectives of relation and manner, as in aquaticus and fanaticus; Greek -atikos is its model.
items.cn: 拉丁 -aticus 构成表示关系与方式的形容词，如 aquaticus、fanaticus；其原型是希腊 -atikos。

items.en: English keeps the suffix as -atic, so enzyme yields enzymatic beside the older enzymic.
items.cn: 英语把该后缀保留为 -atic，于是 enzyme 产生 enzymatic，与较早的 enzymic 并存。

items.en: The adjective appears soon after the noun in late nineteenth-century biochemistry; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 该形容词在 19 世纪后期的生物化学文献中随名词不久出现；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Assays and industrial processes fixed phrases such as enzymatic activity, enzymatic hydrolysis and enzymatic browning.
items.cn: 测定与工业流程固定了 enzymatic activity、enzymatic hydrolysis、enzymatic browning 等搭配。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of the adjective is not recorded, and the choice between the -atic and -ic spellings has never followed a single rule.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词的最早英语书证无确切记录；-atic 与 -ic 两种写法并存的取舍亦无统一规则。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the stem but differ in part of speech or in what they name; group two holds adjectives used in the same experimental sentences.
note.cn: 第一组是共享词干、但词性或所指不同的词；第二组是出现在同一类实验句子中的形容词。

entries.definition: The catalyst itself. Enzymatic only qualifies; a countable thing needs the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指催化剂本身；enzymatic 只是限定语，指可数事物须用名词。

entries.definition: An older synonym of enzymatic, built with -ic. Both qualify the same nouns, but enzymatic is now the common form.
entries.definitionCN: enzymatic 的较早同义词，由 -ic 构成；二者修饰同样的名词，但现在常用 enzymatic。

entries.definition: An inactive enzyme form that must be cut to work; it shares zymē but names a precursor, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 必须被切割才有活性的酶前体；共享 zymē，但指前体而非性质。

entries.definition: A small molecule assisting an enzyme; sharing the stem does not make it an adjective of relation.
entries.definitionCN: 辅助酶的小分子；共享词干并不意味着它是关系形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to catalysis of any kind, including inorganic catalysts; enzymatic specifies that the catalyst is an enzyme.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何催化，包括无机催化剂；enzymatic 明确催化剂是酶。

entries.definition: Relating to hydrolysis, the splitting of bonds by water, which may or may not involve enzymes.
entries.definitionCN: 与水解相关，即用水断键，可能涉及酶，也可能不涉及。

entries.definition: Relating to chemistry in living things generally; enzymatic names only the agent of the reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生物体内的化学；enzymatic 只命名反应的推动者。

entries.definition: The negated form, marking what happens with no enzyme at all; it is a contrast term, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 否定形式，标记完全没有酶时发生的事；是对照词，不是同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: enzyme + -atic: the same relational suffix as in aquatic and dramatic.
normal.cn: enzyme + -atic：与 aquatic、dramatic 中的关系后缀相同。

normal.en: The family runs enzyme, enzymatic, enzymic, enzymatically, enzymology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 enzyme、enzymatic、enzymic、enzymatically、enzymology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: enzymatic reaction, enzymatic hydrolysis, enzymatic activity, enzymatic browning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：酶促反应、酶解、酶活性、酶促褐变。

normal.en: The pair is easy: enzyme is the actor, enzymatic is the way the action is done.
normal.cn: 这组词很好分：enzyme 是行动者，enzymatic 是行动的方式。

normal.en: Food science uses enzymatic browning for the darkening of cut apples and potatoes.
normal.cn: 食品科学用 enzymatic browning 指切开苹果与土豆的变褐。

abstract.en: Picture gloved hands pressing two pieces together, with the glove carrying a small maker's mark.
abstract.cn: 想象戴手套的双手把两块料按到一起，手套上带着小小的制造者标记。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen that uses a living starter instead of a stove.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房用活的酵头代替炉火。

abstract.en: Picture a demolition crew that takes the building apart piece by piece instead of blowing it up.
abstract.cn: 想象一支拆除队把建筑逐块拆下，而不是炸掉。

examples.en: Enzymatic hydrolysis is gentler than acid hydrolysis for food proteins.
examples.cn: 对食品蛋白而言，酶解比酸解更温和。

examples.en: The researchers measured enzymatic activity every ten minutes.
examples.cn: 研究人员每十分钟测定一次酶活性。

examples.en: Enzymatic browning can be slowed by adding lemon juice.
examples.cn: 加入柠檬汁可减缓酶促褐变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「酶（enzyme）＋atic」——带酶属性的、靠酶完成的 → 酶促的、酶解的

root: 希腊 en-「在内」+ zymē「酵素」→ enzyme（1877）+ 拉丁 -aticus（希腊 -atikos）→ enzymatic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one relational suffix: the enzyme is the owner, then the method, then the category, then the measured activity, then cutting, then joining, then removing, and finally the control that lacks it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个表关系的后缀散开：先是所有者，再是方法、类别、被测的活性、切开、接上、清除，最后是缺少它的对照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gloved hands press two pieces together, and the glove carries the catalyst's mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：戴手套的双手把两块料按到一起，手套上带着催化剂的标记。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: the plain relational sense, 'of an enzyme'.
branches.cn: 归属：最朴素的关系义，「酶的」。

branches.en: METHOD AND CLASS: a reaction run by the catalyst, and the whole category so defined.
branches.cn: 方法与类别：由催化剂推动的反应，以及由此定义的整类。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the activity that can be read off an assay.
branches.cn: 测定：可从测定中读出的活性。

branches.en: CUT, JOIN, REMOVE: hydrolysis, synthesis and degradation all use the same adjective.
branches.cn: 切、接、除：酶解、酶法合成与酶促降解共用同一个形容词。

branches.en: CONTROL: the negated form defines the process by what it does without.
branches.cn: 对照：否定形式用「缺少什么」来定义过程。

intro.en: The adjective is the English noun enzyme plus the relational suffix -atic, from Latin -aticus and Greek -atikos.
intro.cn: 该形容词是英语名词 enzyme 加关系后缀 -atic，后者出自拉丁 -aticus 与希腊 -atikos。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix is Latin; the base is Greek plus modern coinage. New Latin enzyma is a re-spelling, not an inherited word.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀是拉丁语；词干是希腊语加现代造词。新拉丁语 enzyma 只是改写拼写，不是传承词。

items.meaning: of an enzyme; done by an enzyme
items.example: The cleavage is entirely enzymatic.
items.exampleCN: 这次切割完全由酶完成。

items.example: The product is enzymatically degraded within hours.
items.exampleCN: 该产物在数小时内被酶促降解。

items.exampleCN: 该酶在四十度以下稳定。

items.example: Enzymic activity was measured in the extract.
items.exampleCN: 提取液中测定了酶活性。

items.example: Modern enzymology began with fermentation.
items.exampleCN: 现代酶学始于发酵研究。

items.example: Non-enzymatic glycation damages proteins.
items.exampleCN: 非酶促糖化会损伤蛋白质。

items.exampleCN: 酶促褐变使切开的水果变坏。

items.exampleCN: 酶法测定需要标准曲线。

definition_zh: 检察官；公诉人；控方律师；（旧）执行者、追究者
definition_en: a lawyer who conducts criminal cases on behalf of the state
core_image: 一名公职律师站在公诉席后，面前是按编号排好的证据袋，身后墙上挂着国徽
scene: 庭审开始，公诉人站起来，先向法官概述证据，再请第一位证人上前。 The prosecutor opened with a summary of the evidence and then called the first witness.
sceneCN: 这里 prosecutor 指代表国家出庭指控被告的检察官（第 1 个义项：代表国家提起公诉的律师）；句意：检察官先概述证据，然后传召第一位证人。图中可辨识物件：公诉席、编号证据袋、国徽、证人席。

pos.zh: 检察官；公诉人（代表国家提起并推进刑事案件的律师）

collocations.zh: 皇家检察官（英联邦用语）

senses.title: The state's lawyer in a criminal case
senses.titleCN: 刑事案件中代表国家的律师
senses.definition: a legal officer who brings and argues the state's case against an accused
senses.definitionCN: 代表国家对被告提起诉讼并出庭论证的公职律师
senses.example: The prosecutor opened with a summary of the evidence and then called the first witness.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官先概述证据，然后传召第一位证人。
senses.why: The agent ending turns the verb of pursuing into a person, so the prosecutor is literally the one who follows the charge forward.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀把「追究」这个动词变成人，所以检察官字面上就是把指控向前追的那个人。

senses.title: The official who decides on charges
senses.definition: the public officer who reviews a file and decides whether to charge
senses.definitionCN: 审阅案卷并决定是否提出指控的公职官员
senses.example: The prosecutor read the file twice before authorising the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官把卷宗读了两遍才批准起诉。
senses.why: Not every accusation reaches court, and the office that screens files holds a gatekeeping power visible in this use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 并非每项指控都能进入法院，负责筛查卷宗的这个职位因此握有把门权，这一含义就体现在这种用法里。

senses.title: The side presenting evidence
senses.definition: the lawyer who presents the evidence against the accused at trial
senses.definitionCN: 在审判中出示不利于被告的证据的律师
senses.example: The prosecutor showed the jury the recording frame by frame.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官逐帧向陪审团展示了那段录像。
senses.why: Because the office speaks first in court, the person is identified with the presentation of proof.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个职位在法庭上先发言，这个人便与证据的呈现紧紧绑在一起。

senses.title: A rank inside a legal system
senses.titleCN: 法律体系内的一个职级
senses.definition: a titled post in a particular system, such as federal or district prosecutor
senses.definitionCN: 特定体系内带名号的职位，如联邦检察官或地区检察官
senses.example: She became the youngest federal prosecutor in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了该地区最年轻的联邦检察官。
senses.why: Different systems grade the office differently, so the word attaches to ranks and jurisdictions rather than to one uniform role.
senses.whyCN: 不同体系给这个职位定的级别不同，所以这个词会附着在级别与辖区上，而不是指一个统一的角色。

senses.title: An old sense: the pursuer or executor
senses.definition: in older texts, one who pursues or carries out an undertaking
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，指追逐或执行某项事业的人
senses.example: The chronicle calls him the prosecutor of the king's justice.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史称他为国王司法事务的执行者。
senses.why: Before the word settled on criminal law, it named anyone who followed a task through to the end, a sense still readable in older prose.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词固定到刑法之前，它指任何把一项任务跟到底的人，这一含义在较早文字中仍可读出。

senses.title: The representative of the public
senses.definition: the official who acts in court for the public rather than for a private client
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上代表公众而非私人委托人行事的人
senses.example: The prosecutor reminded the court that the victim could not speak for herself.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官提醒法庭，受害人已无法为自己发声。
senses.why: The role exists because some wrongs are treated as harms to the whole community, so the lawyer speaks for a collective client.
senses.whyCN: 这个角色之所以存在，是因为某些侵害被视为对共同体的伤害，所以律师代表的是一个集体委托人。

senses.title: Anyone who brings an accusation, loosely
senses.definition: informally, any person or body that presses an accusation
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中，提出指控的任何个人或机构
senses.example: In the complaint the agency appears as prosecutor of the company's conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 在投诉书中，该机构成了公司行为的指控者。
senses.why: The word can leave the courtroom and name whoever is pushing a charge, a looser use common in journalism and campaigning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以走出法庭，指任何推动一项指控的人，这一较松的用法在新闻与倡议文字中很常见。

senses.title: The opposing role in a criminal trial
senses.titleCN: 刑事审判中的对抗角色
senses.definition: the functional opposite of defence counsel in a criminal trial
senses.definitionCN: 刑事审判中与辩方律师相对的功能性角色
senses.example: The prosecutor and defence counsel agreed on the schedule of witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官与辩方律师就证人顺序达成一致。
senses.why: A trial is built as a contest of two offices, and naming one side by its task is the clearest way to mark the other.
senses.whyCN: 审判被搭成两个职位的较量，用任务来命名其中一方，是标记另一方最清楚的办法。

intro.en: Prosecutor is the agent noun of Latin prosequi 'to follow forward', with the agent suffix -or. Latin already had prosecutor for one who pursues, and English narrowed it to the officer who pursues a criminal charge.
intro.cn: prosecutor 是拉丁 prosequi「向前追随」的施事名词，带施事后缀 -or。拉丁语本就有 prosecutor 指「追逐者」，英语把它收窄为追究刑事指控的官员。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it also stands behind sequence and consecutive. In prosequi it supplies the idea of trailing after something until it is reached.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随，也是 sequence 与 consecutive 的来源。在 prosequi 中，它提供「一直尾随直到抵达」的观念。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, to follow forward, to pursue, to continue. Legal usage applied it to the pursuit of a charge.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。法律用法把它用于对指控的追究。

items.en: Latin prosecutor named one who pursues or accompanies, a general agent noun with no special legal rank.
items.cn: 拉丁 prosecutor 指追逐者或随行者，是一般性的施事名词，没有专门的法律级别。

items.en: French legal writing used the corresponding agent noun for the officer conducting a case, and English took the pattern with the rest of its court vocabulary.
items.cn: 法语法律文书用相应的施事名词指推进案件的官员，英语连同其他法庭词汇一起接受了这个模式。

items.en: English prosecutor first meant any pursuer or executor, then settled on the officer who brings the state's criminal case.
items.cn: 英语的 prosecutor 最初指任何追逐者或执行者，后来固定为提起国家刑事案件的官员。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for the courtroom lawyer, for the office that screens charges, and for titled posts such as federal prosecutor.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指庭上的公诉律师、负责筛查指控的机关，以及联邦检察官这类带名号的职位。

note.en: Group one separates the related nouns and verb from a hostile-prefix look-alike and from a mineral-seeker that only sounds similar; group two lists the titles used for the same office in different systems.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根名词与动词、一个带敌对前缀的形近词，以及一个只是读音相近的「找矿者」；第二组列出不同体系对同一职位的称呼。

entries.definition: The proceeding or the team; the prosecutor is the individual lawyer who conducts it.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序或团队；prosecutor 是推进程序的那位律师。

entries.definition: To bring and conduct the case; the prosecutor is the person doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起并推进案件；prosecutor 是做这件事的人。

entries.definition: One who persecutes or harasses, from per- 'through'; the prefix turns following into mistreatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指迫害者、骚扰者，来自 per-「贯穿」；前缀把「跟随」变成「迫害」。

entries.definition: One who searches for minerals, from prospicere 'to look forward'; it looks and sounds close but has no following verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指找矿者，来自 prospicere「向前看」；外形与读音都接近，却没有「跟随」这个动词。

entries.definition: Relating to the office or its practices, not a person who holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 指与该职位或其做法有关的，不是担任者本人。

entries.definition: The elected official who prosecutes cases in a county or district.
entries.definitionCN: 在郡或地区负责起诉的民选官员。

entries.definition: The official who conducts prosecutions for a state or county, a regional variant of the same role.
entries.definitionCN: 为州或郡进行起诉的官员，是同一角色的地区变体。

entries.definition: The prosecutor acting for the Crown in Commonwealth systems.
entries.definitionCN: 在英联邦体系中代表王室起诉的检察官。

entries.definition: A descriptive phrase for the lawyer appearing for the public; prosecutor is the established title.
entries.definitionCN: 对代表公众出庭的律师的描述性说法；prosecutor 是既定称谓。

entries.definition: The collective client on whose behalf the prosecutor acts, not the lawyer.
entries.definitionCN: 指检察官所代表的集体委托人，不是律师本人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real following verb and the real differences between pursuing, harassing and looking forward.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「跟随」动词，以及「追究」「迫害」「向前看」三者之间的真实差别。

normal.en: The prosecutor follows the charge forward; that is what the verb means.
normal.cn: 检察官把指控向前追；这正是那个动词的意思。

normal.en: Persecutor shares the following verb but adds a prefix of 'through': harassment, not litigation.
normal.cn: persecutor 共享「跟随」动词，却加了「贯穿」前缀：那是迫害，不是诉讼。

normal.en: Prospector comes from looking forward, not from following: a miner, not a lawyer.
normal.cn: prospector 来自「向前看」，不是「跟随」：那是找矿人，不是律师。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the office: public prosecutor, federal prosecutor, the prosecutor's office.
normal.cn: 固定说法点明职位：公诉人、联邦检察官、检察官办公室。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

abstract.en: Picture a lawyer standing behind a row of numbered evidence bags, a national emblem on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一位律师站在一排编号证据袋后，墙上挂着国徽。

abstract.en: Picture a gate that most accusations never pass through, kept by one official with a file in hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门，多数指控都过不去，守门者手里拿着一份卷宗。

abstract.en: Picture two seats facing each other, one marked with the public's name, one with a private client's.
abstract.cn: 想象两把相对的椅子，一把写着公众的名字，一把写着私人委托人的名字。

examples.en: The prosecutor must share all exculpatory evidence with the defence.
examples.cn: 检察官必须向辩方披露全部有利于被告的证据。

examples.en: A prosecutor decides whether a file goes forward, not whether the person is guilty.
examples.cn: 检察官决定一份卷宗是否继续推进，而不是决定那个人是否有罪。

examples.en: The prosecutor and the defence lawyer argued over the admissibility of the recording.
examples.cn: 检察官与辩护律师就录音能否采纳展开争论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究特」——把诉状一层层剖开、追到底的那个特别角色 → 检察官

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的施事名词 prosecutor，由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成，词尾 -or 表施事者；英语收窄为「检察官」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the state's courtroom lawyer, through the gatekeeping official, the presenter of evidence, the ranked post, the old pursuer, the voice of the public, the loose accuser, and the opposing role at trial.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从庭上的国家律师开始，经把关官员、证据出示者、有级别的职位、旧时的追行者、公众的代言人、泛称的指控者，最后到审判中的对抗角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lawyer behind numbered evidence bags, an emblem on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位律师站在编号证据袋后，墙上挂着徽记。

branches.en: THE LAWYER: the agent of the charge, the one who follows it through court.
branches.cn: 律师：指控的执行者，把它一路追过法庭的人。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: screening files and holding a rank are the same post seen from inside the system.
branches.cn: 职位：筛查卷宗与占据级别，是同一职位在体系内部的两种看法。

branches.en: THE VOICE: presenting proof in court and pressing an accusation outside it both mean speaking for a charge.
branches.cn: 声音：在庭上出示证据、在庭外推动指控，都是替一项指控发声。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: before criminal law claimed the word, a prosecutor was simply one who carried a task through.
branches.cn: 旧义：刑法接管这个词之前，检察官只是把一项任务执行到底的人。

branches.en: THE COUNTERPART: the office speaks for the public and therefore stands opposite the defence.
branches.cn: 对应面：这个职位替公众发声，因此与辩方相对而立。

intro.en: Prosecutor is a Latin agent noun on a verb of following, and its ending is what makes it a person rather than a process.
intro.cn: prosecutor 是建立在「跟随」动词上的拉丁施事名词，词尾正是它成为人而非过程的原因。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are pro- 'forth', sequi 'follow' and -or 'one who'; Latin already formed prosecutor from them, and English kept the shape.
latinIntro.cn: 构件是 pro-「向前」、sequi「跟随」与 -or「做某事的人」；拉丁语已用它们构成 prosecutor，英语保留了这一形态。

items.meaningCN: 向前、向外（前缀给跟随指定方向）
items.example: The prefix points the following forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把跟随指向前方。

items.example: The verb names the following.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名跟随。

items.example: The compound named the pursuit.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名追究。

items.meaningCN: 执行动作的人（施事后缀把动作转成施事者）
items.example: Doctor and victor share the ending.
items.exampleCN: doctor 与 victor 共享这个词尾。

items.meaningCN: 追究指控的人（由过程转为职责承担者）
items.example: The prosecutor filed the charge.
items.exampleCN: 检察官提出了指控。

items.meaningCN: 对指控的追究（名词后缀把动作转成程序）
items.example: The prosecution lasted months.
items.exampleCN: 这场起诉持续了数月。

items.meaning: to bring and conduct a case
items.meaningCN: 提起并推进案件（回到动作本身）
items.example: They chose to prosecute.
items.exampleCN: 他们选择起诉。

items.meaningCN: 与该职位有关的（形容词后缀把角色转成属性）
items.example: Prosecutorial review is required.
items.exampleCN: 需要检察官审查。

definition_zh: 以研究为依据的；建立在系统调查与证据之上的
definition_en: built on systematic investigation and evidence rather than on opinion, tradition or guesswork
core_image: 一份课程方案旁摊着三篇同行评审论文，每处主张都用高亮线连到同一张数据表
scene: 一所学校在改教材之前，先让教师把近十年的课堂实验报告摊在桌上逐条对照。 Their new reading programme is entirely research-based.
sceneCN: 学校在改教材前把多年课堂实验报告逐条对照，新方案完全建立在研究证据上；句中的 research-based 指「以系统调查为依据的」（第 1 个义项：建立在系统研究而非意见之上）。图中可辨识物件：课程方案、论文抽印本、数据表、荧光笔。

pos.zh: 以研究为依据的；基于证据的

forms.label: 分词式写法（不带连字符）

senses.title: Founded on systematic inquiry
senses.definition: built on organised investigation rather than on opinion or habit
senses.definitionCN: 以有组织的调查为基础，而非依据意见或习惯
senses.example: Their new reading programme is entirely research-based.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的新阅读方案完全以研究为依据。
senses.why: the compound simply joins the noun research, which names organised inquiry, to based, which marks a foundation.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把表示有组织调查的名词 research 与表示「以……为基础」的 based 直接接在一起。

senses.title: Evidence for classroom practice
senses.definition: describing teaching methods chosen because studies show they work
senses.definitionCN: 指因研究显示有效而被选用的教学方法
senses.example: The district now prefers research-based instruction over handed-down routines.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区如今更倾向基于研究的教学，而非沿袭旧例。
senses.why: education borrowed the compound because classroom tradition can be defended by custom alone, and the word insists on tested support.
senses.whyCN: 教育界借用这个复合词，因为课堂传统往往只能靠习惯辩护，而这个词坚持要有经过检验的支持。

senses.title: Grounded in clinical trials
senses.definition: describing medical advice that rests on controlled trials and published outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 指建立在对照试验与已发表结果之上的医学建议
senses.example: Only research-based treatments are covered by the new guideline.
senses.exampleCN: 新指南只纳入以临床试验为依据的疗法。
senses.why: medicine supplied the earliest strict use, since a drug must show measured results before it can be recommended.
senses.whyCN: 医学提供了最早也最严格的用法，因为药物必须先拿出测量结果才能被推荐。

senses.title: A claim with citations
senses.definition: describing a statement that can be traced to published studies
senses.definitionCN: 指可追溯到已发表研究的主张
senses.example: The brief is research-based, so every figure carries a citation.
senses.exampleCN: 这份简报有研究依据，每个数字都带着出处。
senses.why: the word pushes a claim from assertion to traceable statement, which is why citations follow it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把主张从「断言」推成「可追溯的陈述」，因此它后面常跟着引文。

senses.title: A method drawn from trials
senses.titleCN: 由实证试验得出的方法
senses.definition: describing a procedure developed and revised through repeated testing
senses.definitionCN: 指经反复试验开发并修正的程序
senses.example: Their soil treatment is research-based and was retested on three farms.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的土壤处理法基于实证研究，并已在三处农场复测。
senses.why: a method earns the label only after trials, so the compound implies a history of revision behind the procedure.
senses.whyCN: 方法要经过试验才配得上这个标签，因此复合词隐含了这套程序背后的修订史。

senses.title: Against anecdotal practice
senses.titleCN: 与凭经验传闻的做法相对
senses.definition: used to contrast tested practice with advice drawn from single stories
senses.definitionCN: 用于把经过检验的做法与凭个别故事得出的建议相对照
senses.example: The clinic replaced anecdotal habits with research-based protocols.
senses.exampleCN: 该诊所用以研究为依据的规程取代了凭传闻的习惯。
senses.why: the opposition to anecdote is built into the word: research means many cases measured, anecdote means one case remembered.
senses.whyCN: 与轶事的对立内置于词中：研究意味着测量许多案例，轶事意味着记住一个案例。

senses.title: Driven by company research
senses.definition: describing a product decision that rests on the firm's own laboratory work
senses.definitionCN: 指建立在企业自身实验工作的产品决策
senses.example: The formula is research-based and protected by two patents.
senses.exampleCN: 这个配方由研发支撑，并受两项专利保护。
senses.why: industry uses the same compound for internal laboratories, where the evidence is produced by the company itself.
senses.whyCN: 产业界把同一复合词用于内部实验室，此时证据由企业自己生产。

senses.title: Tested with users
senses.definition: describing a design shaped by observed user behaviour and measured results
senses.definitionCN: 指依据观察到的用户行为与测量结果来塑造的设计
senses.example: The interface is research-based, built from months of usability sessions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个界面以研究为依据，来自数月的可用性测试。
senses.why: design extended the compound to any product shaped by observation, because watching users is a form of research too.
senses.whyCN: 设计领域把这个复合词扩展到一切由观察塑造的产品，因为观察用户也是一种研究。

intro.en: The adjective joins research, which came through Old French from the Latin verb circare 'to go about, explore', and based, which comes from Latin basis and Greek basis 'step, pedestal'. The compound itself is a modern formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由 research 与 based 组合而成。research 经古法语来自拉丁动词 circare「四处走动、探查」；based 来自拉丁 basis 与希腊 basis「台阶、基座」。复合词本身是近代构造。年代为约数。

items.en: Circare meant 'to go about, to wander around searching'. It came from circus 'circle', so the original picture is someone tracing a circle while looking for something.
items.cn: circare 意为「四处走动、搜寻」，来自 circus「圆圈」，因此最初的意象是循着圈子寻找东西。

items.en: Old French added an intensive re- to cerchier 'to search' and produced recerche, the act of searching thoroughly.
items.cn: 古法语在 cerchier「搜寻」前加起强化作用的 re-，构成 recerche，即彻底搜寻的行为。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the fifteenth century, first as the act of searching for a person or thing, then as systematic study.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入该词，最初指寻找某人某物，后来指系统的研究。

items.en: Basis meant 'step, pedestal, foundation' in Greek and passed into Latin unchanged in meaning; French base gave English the noun base.
items.cn: basis 在希腊语中意为「台阶、基座、基础」，进入拉丁语后意义不变；法语 base 给英语提供了名词 base。

items.en: Research-based appears in the twentieth century as a hyphenated compound, first in medicine and then in education and policy, wherever a decision needs documented support.
items.cn: research-based 于二十世纪作为带连字符的复合词出现，先用于医学，继而用于教育与政策，凡需要文献支持作决定之处都用它。

items.en: The further origin of circus and of Greek basis is uncertain; the commonly cited links to a root meaning 'to turn' and to a verb meaning 'to step' are reconstructions rather than established derivations.
items.cn: circus 与希腊 basis 的更早来源不确定；常被引用的、与表示「转动」的词根及表示「迈步」的动词之间的联系属于重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds the parts of the compound and words that look close to them; group two holds labels for kinds of evidence, which differ in what counts as proof.
note.cn: 第一组是复合词的组成部分及形近词；第二组是各类「证据」标签，区别在于什么算作证明。

entries.definition: The activity of organised inquiry; the compound only says a thing rests on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指有组织的探究活动本身；复合词只说明某物以它为基础。

entries.definition: The person who carries out the inquiry, not a description of the thing built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事探究的人，而非对「以其为基础之物」的描述。

entries.definition: Looks like the second half of research but lacks the intensive prefix, and means a plain hunt.
entries.definitionCN: 形似 research 的后半，却少了那个强化前缀，只表示普通的搜寻。

entries.definition: Begins with the same re- sound but belongs to certify, with no connection to inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 开头是同样的 re- 音，却属于 certify，与探究毫无关系。

entries.definition: Names the proof itself; research-based names the activity that produced the proof.
entries.definitionCN: 直接点明「证明」，而 research-based 点明产生证明的活动。

entries.definition: Says knowledge comes from observation and experiment, without implying a body of studies.
entries.definitionCN: 指知识来自观察与实验，但不暗示已有一批研究。

entries.definition: Stresses that decisions follow measured numbers, which may come from routine tracking rather than inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 强调决策跟着测量数字走，而这些数字可能来自日常记录而非研究。

entries.definition: The opposite pole: evidence from a single remembered case, not from systematic study.
entries.definitionCN: 相反的一极：证据来自一个被记住的个案，而非系统研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the two real halves of the compound, its real family and its real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自复合词真实的两半、真实词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: re- 'again, thoroughly' plus cerchier 'to search': to search thoroughly.
normal.cn: re-「再、彻底」加 cerchier「搜寻」：彻底搜寻。

normal.en: research plus based: something standing on a foundation of inquiry.
normal.cn: research 加 based：某物立在探究的地基上。

normal.en: The family runs research, researcher, researchable, under-researched.
normal.cn: 词族包括 research、researcher、researchable、under-researched。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: research-based policy, research-based instruction, research-based medicine.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：基于研究的政策、基于研究的教学、循证医学。

normal.en: The contrast with anecdotal advice keeps the meaning sharp.
normal.cn: 与凭轶事给出的建议对照，词义才清楚。

abstract.en: Picture a table with one leg resting on a stack of journals instead of on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，一条桌腿不落在地面，而落在一摞期刊上。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe card with a footnote longer than the recipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一张食谱卡，脚注比食谱本身还长。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge whose every plank is stamped with the date it was tested.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，每块木板都盖着测试日期的印。

examples.en: The tutoring model is research-based and was piloted in twelve schools.
examples.cn: 这套辅导模式以研究为依据，并已在十二所学校试点。

examples.en: A research-based claim can be checked; a slogan cannot.
examples.cn: 以研究为依据的主张可以被核查，口号则不能。

examples.en: The hospital moved to research-based protocols for wound care.
examples.cn: 这家医院改用基于研究的伤口护理规程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「research（研究）+ based（以……为基础）」——把结论建立在研究上 → 以研究为依据的

root: 拉丁 circare「四处探寻」→ 古法语 recerche「彻底搜寻」→ 英语 research；拉丁 basis／希腊 basis「基座」→ 法语 base → 英语 based；二者在二十世纪组成复合形容词。circus 与 basis 的更深来源不确定，常见词根联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses keep one frame: an organised inquiry sits underneath a decision, and the frame is then filled by classrooms, clinics, citations, trials, company labs and tested designs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用一个框架：有组织的探究垫在某个决定之下；这个框架再被课堂、诊所、引文、试验、企业实验室与被测试的设计逐一填满。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document standing on a thick stack of study reports instead of on thin air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文件立在厚厚一摞研究报告上，而不是悬在空中。

branches.en: FOUNDATION AND CLASSROOM: the compound first says 'resting on inquiry', then says which room the inquiry serves.
branches.cn: 地基与课堂：复合词先说「立在探究上」，再说这份探究服务哪个场所。

branches.en: CLINIC AND CITATION: strict medical use demands trials, and written use demands traceable sources.
branches.cn: 诊所与引文：严格的医学用法要求试验，书面用法要求可追溯的出处。

branches.en: TRIAL AND CONTRAST: a method earns the label through retesting, and the label sharpens against mere anecdote.
branches.cn: 试验与对照：方法经复测才获得标签，而标签在与轶事的对照中变锋利。

branches.en: COMPANY LAB: the evidence can come from the firm's own bench rather than from public studies.
branches.cn: 企业实验室：证据可以来自企业自己的实验台，而非公开研究。

branches.en: OBSERVED USE: design extends 'research' to watching how people actually behave with a product.
branches.cn: 观察到的使用：设计领域把「研究」扩展到观察人如何使用产品。

intro.en: The compound is transparent: one half names the inquiry, the other half names the foundation, and both halves have their own Latin and Greek histories.
intro.cn: 这个复合词是透明的：一半点明探究，一半点明地基，两半各有自己的拉丁与希腊来历。

latinIntro.en: Latin circare supplies research through Old French; Latin basis, from Greek basis, supplies base and based.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 circare 经古法语提供 research；拉丁 basis（源自希腊 basis）提供 base 与 based。

items.example: The prefix intensifies the search.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀强化了「搜寻」这一动作。

items.example: Circare came from the word for a circle.
items.exampleCN: circare 来自表示「圆圈」的词。

items.example: Research precedes the compound.
items.exampleCN: 研究先于复合词存在。

items.example: The base is what the claim stands on.
items.exampleCN: 基础就是主张所立之处。

items.example: The second half marks the foundation.
items.exampleCN: 后半标示地基。

items.example: A researcher gathered the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 研究者收集了证据。

items.example: The question is researchable.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题可以被研究。

items.example: The condition remains under-researched.
items.exampleCN: 这种情况仍研究不足。

items.example: The programme is research-based.
items.exampleCN: 该方案以研究为依据。

definition_zh: 开始存在；产生；成立；形成；问世
definition_en: to begin to be, whether of an institution, a species, a rule, an idea or an object
core_image: 一间空屋子的门被推开，桌上先出现一张纸，纸上写着第一个名字，随后又添了第二张、第三张
scene: 档案馆里，一份旧会议记录显示，这个机构最初只是几个人在租来的房间里议事，后来才正式成立。 The bureau may come into existence as a temporary office before it wins permanent funding.
sceneCN: 这里指机构开始存在、正式设立（第 1 个义项：组织从无到有地成立）；句意为该局可能先以临时办事处的形式设立，之后才获得长期经费。图中可辨识物件：租来的房间、会议记录、临时门牌、经费批文。

pos.zh: 开始存在；产生（不及物动词短语，主语为被产生的事物）
成立；问世（用于机构、制度、作品）

collocations.phrase: come into existence under a new law

derivatives.zh: 短语中的核心名词，义为「存在；生存」
由名词回构的动词，义为「存在；生存」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「存在的；现存的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「现有的」

senses.title: An organisation is founded
senses.definition: to begin to operate as an organised body
senses.definitionCN: 作为有组织的机构开始运转
senses.example: The first public library in the town may come into existence only after a large gift.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的第一座公共图书馆，可能只在一笔大额捐赠之后才会成立。
senses.why: Coming is movement toward a place; existence is the place reached, so founding is the moment the thing arrives.
senses.whyCN: 「来」是朝某处移动，「存在」是抵达之处，因此「成立」就是那件事物到达的时刻。

senses.title: A species appears
senses.definition: to arise as a new kind of living thing
senses.definitionCN: 作为一种新的生物类别出现
senses.example: New species can come into existence when a river separates two populations for ages.
senses.exampleCN: 当一条河把两个种群隔开很久，新的物种就可能出现。
senses.why: A new kind arrives at standing on its own when a river keeps two populations apart.
senses.whyCN: 一条河把两个种群隔开，新的一类就来到独立站住的位置。

senses.title: A law takes effect
senses.definition: to begin to have legal force
senses.definitionCN: 开始具有法律效力
senses.example: The rule should come into existence only after the council publishes it.
senses.exampleCN: 该规则只有在议会公布之后才应产生效力。
senses.why: A rule stands forth only when it is published and begins to hold.
senses.whyCN: 规则在公布并开始生效时才站出来。

senses.title: An idea takes shape
senses.definition: to emerge as a recognisable concept
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个可辨认的概念出现
senses.example: The notion of a common market can come into existence long before any treaty is signed.
senses.exampleCN: 共同市场的观念可以在任何条约签署之前很久就已形成。
senses.why: A concept stands forth in speech long before it stands in a treaty.
senses.whyCN: 观念先在言语中站出来，远早于它在条约中站住。

senses.title: A work appears
senses.definition: to be produced and become available as a text or an object
senses.definitionCN: 作为文本或实物被产出并可供人接触
senses.example: The manuscript may come into existence as a set of loose notes before it becomes a book.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手稿可能先以一组散页笔记的形式出现，然后才成为一本书。
senses.why: Loose notes stand forth as a book when they are gathered into one body.
senses.whyCN: 散页在被收拢成一体时，作为一本书站出来。

senses.title: A celestial body forms
senses.definition: to condense or assemble as a physical body in space
senses.definitionCN: 在太空中凝聚或聚合成一个天体
senses.example: A star can come into existence from a cloud of gas and dust.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗恒星可以由一团气体与尘埃形成。
senses.why: Gas and dust arrive at standing as a star when gravity gathers them.
senses.whyCN: 气体与尘埃在引力收拢时，来到作为恒星站住的位置。

senses.title: A word enters the language
senses.definition: to be coined and begin to be used by speakers
senses.definitionCN: 被造出并开始被使用者采用
senses.example: Most slang terms come into existence in speech and reach print much later.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数俚语先在口语里产生，很久以后才进入印刷品。
senses.why: A slang term stands forth in speech and only later stands in print.
senses.whyCN: 俚语先在口语中站出来，之后才站进印刷品。

senses.title: A post is created
senses.definition: to be established as an office or a position
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个职位或岗位被设立
senses.example: The office of inspector should come into existence when the factory opens.
senses.exampleCN: 监察员这一职位应在工厂开工时设立。
senses.why: A post stands forth when an office is written into the rules.
senses.whyCN: 当职位被写进规则，它就站出来了。

senses.title: A relationship forms
senses.definition: to develop as a working relationship or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 作为一种可运作的关系或局面发展出来
senses.example: A working trust can come into existence only after both sides keep small promises.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当双方都守住了小的承诺，可用的信任才会形成。
senses.why: Trust stands forth only after small promises have stood.
senses.whyCN: 只有小的承诺先站住，信任才站出来。

intro.en: The phrase combines a native verb of arriving with a noun built in Latin from out plus standing. What comes into existence literally arrives at standing outside nothing.
intro.cn: 这个短语把本族表示「到来」的动词，与拉丁语用「向外」加「站立」构成的名词配在一起。所谓进入存在，字面就是「来到外面的站立之处」。

items.en: Cuman meant to come or to arrive, and it is one of the oldest verbs in English.
items.cn: 这个词意为「来、到达」，是英语中最古老的动词之一。

items.en: Sistere meant to stand or to hold one's ground, the standing image shared by the whole family.
items.cn: 这个词意为「站立、站住脚」，是整个词族共享的「站立」意象。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus sistere produced exsistere, to stand forth, to appear, to be.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀加「站立」，构成「站出来、显现、存在」的动词。

items.en: The noun named the state of standing forth, and French and English took it as existence.
items.cn: 相应的名词指「站出来的状态」，法语与英语把它用作「存在」。

items.era: PHRASE FIXED IN THE SIXTEENTH CENTURY
items.en: The frame with come fixed in the sixteenth century for institutions and laws, and later for species and stars. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 与「来」搭配的框架在十六世纪固定下来，先用于机构与法律，后扩及物种与星体。最早书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin standing noun; the second group holds other ways of saying that something began to be.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「站立」名词；第二组是其他表示「开始存在」的说法。

entries.definition: The noun names the state of being; the phrase names the moment of arriving at that state.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「存在的状态」；短语指「抵达这一状态的那一刻」。

entries.definition: The verb says that something is; it does not mark the beginning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词只陈述某物存在，并不标出「开始」这一点。

entries.definition: It describes what already is; the phrase is about the step before it existed.
entries.definitionCN: 它形容已经存在的东西；短语说的则是它尚未存在之前的那一步。

entries.definition: It marks what is present now, often before a change; it has no sense of origin.
entries.definitionCN: 标出现在已有之物，常用在变化之前；不含起源之意。

entries.definition: Nearly the same in meaning, but it sounds more literary and is used less for offices and budgets.
entries.definitionCN: 意思几乎相同，但更带文学色彩，较少用于职位与预算。

entries.definition: Often used for problems, questions and situations that appear without a maker.
entries.definitionCN: 常用于没有明确制造者的问题、疑问与局面。

entries.definition: It stresses becoming visible after being unnoticed, as a pattern emerging from data.
entries.definitionCN: 强调从未被注意的状态中显现，如规律从数据中浮现。

entries.definition: It implies a deliberate founder, which the phrase itself does not require.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示有人有意设立，而本短语本身并不要求有创立者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the empty room, the river splitting a population, the published rule and the first star.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用空房间、把种群隔开的河、公布的规则与第一颗星四个场景。

normal.en: An empty room, then one sheet of paper with the first name on it.
normal.cn: 空房间里先出现一张纸，上面写着第一个名字。

normal.en: A river wide enough to keep two herds apart for thousands of years.
normal.cn: 一条宽到能把两群动物隔开上千年的河。

normal.en: A rule that exists on paper but has no force until it is published.
normal.cn: 一条只写在纸上、公布之前毫无效力的规则。

normal.en: Gas and dust collapsing until a point of light switches on.
normal.cn: 气体与尘埃塌缩，直到一点光亮起来。

normal.en: A slang word spoken at a market stall decades before it is printed.
normal.cn: 一个俚语在集市摊上被说了几十年，才被印出来。

abstract.en: Existence begins as an event, not as a substance.
abstract.cn: 存在是从一个事件开始的，而不是从一种实体开始的。

abstract.en: Institutions are the slowest kind of new thing: they must be born in rooms before they are born in law.
abstract.cn: 机构是最慢的一种新事物：先在房间里出生，才在法律里出生。

abstract.en: Nothing begins alone: a river, a gift or a kept promise is always part of the story.
abstract.cn: 没有东西是独自开始的：一条河、一笔捐赠或一个守住的承诺，总在故事里。

examples.en: A new department may come into existence only after the budget is approved.
examples.cn: 新部门可能只有在预算获批之后才会设立。

examples.en: Written records can come into existence long before a formal archive is founded.
examples.cn: 书面记录可以在正式档案馆成立之前很久就已产生。

examples.en: The custom may come into existence among sailors and spread inland later.
examples.cn: 这一习俗可能先在船员中形成，后来才传到内陆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「康姆 因图 伊克斯伊斯坦斯」：把「来到站立之处」记成一间空屋里先出现一张写着名字的纸——名字落纸，事物就开始了

root: 前半为本族动词，意为「来、到达」；后半名词出自拉丁语，由表示「向外」的前缀加表示「站立」的词根构成，本义是「站出来、显现」。短语整体表示「某物从无到有地开始站立存在」，不点明是否有创立者。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin something: a body, a species, a law, an idea, a text, a star, a word, a post, and a trust.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都让某物开始：机构、物种、法律、观念、文本、恒星、词语、职位与信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty room, and then a single sheet of paper carrying the first name, followed by more sheets.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间空屋子，然后出现一张写着第一个名字的纸，接着是更多张。

branches.en: THE FOUNDED THING: a bureau or an inspectorship is written into being.
branches.cn: 被设立之物：一个局或一个监察职位被写出来而存在。

branches.en: THE NATURAL BIRTH: a species splits off, a star condenses.
branches.cn: 自然诞生：物种分化，恒星凝聚。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE IDEA: force begins on publication, a concept forms before any treaty.
branches.cn: 规则与观念：效力始于公布，观念在条约之前形成。

branches.en: THE TEXT AND THE WORD: loose notes become a book, slang reaches print late.
branches.cn: 文本与词语：散页成为书，俚语很晚才入印刷。

branches.en: THE KEPT PROMISE: trust forms only after small promises hold.
branches.cn: 守住的承诺：信任只在小的承诺兑现后形成。

intro.en: The phrase joins a native arriving verb to a Latin noun of standing forth; the endings build the verb of being and its descriptions.
intro.cn: 这个短语把本族「到达」动词与拉丁语「站出来」名词结合；词尾造出「存在」动词及其描述形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin exsistere and exsistentia reached French and then English, which shortened the noun to its modern form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「显现」动词与名词进入法语，再进入英语，英语把名词缩成现代形式。

items.example: It marks the thing as standing forth.
items.exampleCN: 它标出某物「站出来」。

items.example: The standing verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 名词背后的「站立」动词。

items.example: The direct source of the verb of being.
items.exampleCN: 「存在」动词的直接来源。

items.example: The noun English shortened.
items.exampleCN: 英语加以缩短的那个名词。

items.example: It carries the noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它承担表示状态的名词。

items.example: It forms the adjective of what is.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「存在者」的形容词。

items.example: It forms the participle of what currently is.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「现有」的分词。

items.example: It marks arrival at the new state.
items.exampleCN: 它标出抵达新状态。
